_about: The complete syllabus per dance, following BallroomDancers.com (figure names, levels, order and links are theirs; summaries and tips are our own words). status: playable = danced in the game (game_id); same_as = same steps as another playable variant; chart_only = charted but not yet danceable in the game; no_chart = the site has no chart.

std_waltz.name: Slow Waltz
std_waltz.music: Slow, flowing three-four music such as ballads and orchestral pieces, with a clear stress on the first beat of each bar.
std_waltz.movement_tip: Lower into the standing knee as you step on 1, grow taller through 2 and 3 and settle at the end of the bar, letting the bodies swing like a pendulum with sway into each turn. Walk forward through the heel and back through the toe.
std_waltz.position_tip: Stand in a settled closed hold, slightly offset so each partner's right foot points between the other's feet, with the joined hands near her eye level and his right hand on her shoulder blade. Keep the frame quiet and lead with the body rather than the arms.

figures.name: Closed Changes
figures.summary: Two three-step changes danced without turn that swap the free foot, so the couple can alternate between natural and reverse turning figures.
figures.tip: Keep step 2 to the side and let the swing carry it slightly forward; use the right-foot change after a Natural Turn into a Reverse Turn, Whisk or Telemark, and the left-foot change after a Reverse Turn into a Natural, Spin Turn or Hesitation Change.

figures.name: Natural Turn
figures.summary: The basic right-turning figure: two bars of forward-side-close and back-side-close that rotate three-quarters to the right along the line of dance.
figures.tip: Start it facing diagonal wall after a left-foot Closed Change, Chasse from Promenade or Outside Change and finish facing diagonal centre for the right-foot Closed Change; at a corner, go into a Spin Turn or another Natural.

figures.name: Reverse Turn
figures.summary: The basic left-turning figure, the mirror image of the Natural Turn: forward-side-close and back-side-close turning three-quarters to the left.
figures.tip: Begin facing diagonal centre after the right-foot Closed Change or a Hesitation Change, and end facing diagonal wall ready for the left-foot Closed Change, a Whisk or a Double Reverse Spin.

figures.name: Natural Spin Turn
figures.summary: A Natural Turn whose second half becomes a pivot and a forward drive, turning more than a full rotation; ideal for corners.
figures.tip: Keep your right thigh close to hers through the pivot; enter from a Natural Turn at a corner, a Chasse from Promenade or an Outside Change, and leave with the back half of a Reverse Turn, a Reverse Corte or a Basic Weave.

figures.summary: A three-step figure that opens the couple from closed hold into promenade by crossing the left foot behind on 3.
figures.tip: Rise and sway left as the left foot hooks behind, and open her with your body rather than your arm; dance it after a Reverse Turn or Closed Change and follow it with a Chasse from Promenade, Wing or Cross Hesitation.

figures.name: Chasse from Promenade Position
figures.summary: A travelling side chasse from promenade that brings the couple back to closed hold, ready to step outside partner.
figures.tip: Count it 1, 2-and-3 and keep the chasse compact; it follows a Whisk, Back Whisk or Open Telemark and flows into a Natural Turn, Spin Turn or Hesitation Change taken outside partner.

figures.name: Closed Impetus
figures.summary: A right-turning figure where the man turns on his heel while the lady travels round him, usually after the first half of a Natural Turn.
figures.tip: Keep the closing foot light and stay low until the feet meet; it follows a Back Lock, Progressive Chasse to Right or Drag Hesitation and leads into a Reverse Corte, Left Whisk or Hover Corte.

preceded_by.name: Reverse Corte

figures.name: Hesitation Change
figures.summary: Half a Natural Turn followed by a bar with no rise and a heel pull, used to change from natural to reverse turning without a closed change.
figures.tip: Stay down on the second bar and keep the left foot free; it suits a corner after a Natural Turn or Chasse from Promenade and goes straight into a Reverse Turn, Telemark or Drag Hesitation.

figures.name: Double Reverse Spin
figures.summary: A quick left-turning spin in which the man turns on his toes while the lady makes a heel turn and crosses her feet.
figures.tip: Keep the feet together and let the body finish the turn over 2-3; it comes after a Reverse Turn, Closed Change or Hesitation Change and leads into a Whisk, a Closed Change or a Progressive Chasse to Right.

variants.title: Double Reverse Spin
variants.reason: The site's lady chart has a foot error on step 2: she steps back on the right foot and the next row closes the right foot again (it should be the left foot closing for her heel turn). A correct conversion therefore fails the chart-fidelity check; it can be made playable once the chart row is corrected.

figures.name: Reverse Pivot
figures.summary: A single quick pivot to the left on the man's right foot, taken on the 'and' borrowed from the bar before, used to redirect the couple.
figures.tip: Keep the step small with the left foot held in front; it follows a Natural Spin Turn or Closed Impetus and turns into a Reverse Turn, Whisk, Telemark or Double Reverse Spin.

variants.title: Reverse Pivot
variants.reason: One half-beat pivot counted '&' that takes its time from the previous bar; game figures must fill whole 3/4 bars, so it cannot stand alone as a figure.

figures.tip: Keep the hips going forward and the cross tight; it follows a Chasse from Promenade, Outside Change or Basic Weave and leads into a Natural Turn, Spin Turn or Hesitation Change taken outside partner.

figures.name: Wing
figures.summary: From promenade the man steps through and closes slowly while the lady walks round his left side.
figures.tip: Turn the upper body left gradually over 2-3 to draw her round; it follows a Whisk or Open Telemark and leads into a Reverse Turn, Telemark, Progressive Chasse to Right or Fallaway Reverse.

figures.name: Outside Spin
figures.summary: A compact right-turning spin begun with a toe-turned-in pivot as the lady steps outside, turning a whole rotation (or three-quarters when underturned).
figures.tip: Keep the first step small and stay over your feet; it follows a Reverse Corte, Cross Hesitation or Hover Corte and leads into a Natural Turn, Spin Turn or Hesitation Change, or underturned into a Reverse Corte.

figures.name: Turning Lock to Left
figures.summary: A backward lock that turns left and ends with the man ready to step outside partner, or open in promenade.
figures.tip: Lead the lock with the right side and turn only on the last step; dance it after a Natural Spin Turn and follow with a Natural Turn, Spin Turn or Hesitation Change, or with a Cross Hesitation in the promenade version.

figures.name: Drag Hesitation
figures.summary: A left-turning bar in which the man drags the left foot in without weight, ending ready to move backward with the lady outside.
figures.tip: Rise late on 2 and let the drag fill beat 3; it follows a Closed Change, Hesitation Change or Wing and leads into a Back Lock, Closed Impetus or Outside Change.

figures.name: Left Whisk

figures.name: Contra Check

std_foxtrot.name: Slow Foxtrot
std_foxtrot.music: Unhurried swing or big-band jazz in four, played with a relaxed, crooning feel.
std_foxtrot.movement_tip: Travel on long, low strides that never stop between steps: forward walks land on the heel, backward walks on the toe, and the rise and sway stay gentle so slow-quick-quick flows as one line.
std_foxtrot.position_tip: Use a normal Standard closed hold with the lady a little to the man's right, a wide, steady frame and light body contact so the couple moves as one.

figures.tip: Open the dance with a preparation step and a Feather; it also comes after a Three Step, Natural Turn or Change of Direction and runs naturally into a Reverse Turn, Three Step or Change of Direction.

std_tango.name: Tango
std_tango.music: Orchestral tango with a crisp, marching pulse, where the beat is clipped and sharp rather than flowing.
std_tango.movement_tip: Keep the knees softly flexed and the body level, with no rise and fall at all. Lift the feet slightly and place them so each step lands crisply instead of gliding.
std_tango.position_tip: The hold is more compact than in the other Standard dances, with her further to his right and his right hand a little lower on her back. Keep the frame still and let the legs do the work.

figures.name: Basic Walks
figures.summary: The tango walk is the building block of the dance: a left and a right foot walk, each a slow, placed step that curves gently to the left. The walk on the right foot can also end in promenade, a short way into promenade without a Progressive Link.
figures.tip: Keep the knees flexed and place each foot rather than swinging it; after the right foot walk the left foot is free for a Progressive Side Step, a Progressive Link or an Open Reverse Turn.

figures.name: Progressive Side Step
figures.summary: Three steps, quick quick slow, that travel the couple forward with a short side step in the middle; with a right foot walk before it, it is the nearest thing tango has to a basic.
figures.tip: Keep the side step short and slightly back; dance it after a right foot walk and follow it with a Rock Turn (from its second step) or another walk.

figures.name: Progressive Link
figures.summary: Two quick steps that open the couple from closed hold into promenade, the door to every promenade figure.
figures.tip: Turn her with your body on the second quick rather than pushing with the arms; follow it with a Closed Promenade, Open Promenade or Natural Twist Turn.

figures.summary: A Four Step with an extra small back step and a dramatic weightless placement into promenade on the slow.

figures.name: Contra Check
figures.summary: A sharp checked action forward for the man with flexed knees, recovering and opening into promenade.
figures.tip: Make the check from the leg, not the shoulders; follow it with a Closed Promenade or another promenade figure.

quickstep.name: Quickstep
quickstep.music: Bright, fast swing and big-band jazz with a crisp four-beat pulse.
quickstep.movement_tip: Glide around the room with long swinging steps, then stay high on the balls of the feet for the quick chasses and locks and lower softly at the end of each slow.
quickstep.position_tip: Hold a closed Standard frame with the lady slightly to your right and your bodies lightly connected, so the fast footwork moves as one unit.

figures.name: Quarter Turn to Right
figures.summary: A four-step right-turning starter, slow-quick-quick-slow, taking the couple from facing diagonal wall to backing diagonal centre. It is the usual opening figure and the partner of the Progressive Chasse.
figures.tip: Close the feet firmly on the second quick and keep the last slow sideways, then carry straight on into a Progressive Chasse, a Reverse Pivot or a Hover Corte.

figures.name: Progressive Chasse
figures.summary: A left-turning chasse from backing diagonal centre to facing diagonal wall, ready for a step outside partner; with the Quarter Turn to Right it zigzags down the room. The checked version stops at a corner and backs out along the new wall.
figures.tip: Think back, side, together, side with the feet touching on the close, then go into a Forward Lock, Natural Spin Turn or Natural Turn with Hesitation; near a corner use the checked version instead.

figures.tip: The tipsy sway toward the travel is optional, so keep the chasse compact and come out with the lock; afterwards dance a Natural Spin Turn, Forward Lock or Quarter Turn to Right.

variants.title: Overturned Tipple Chasse
variants.reason: The site's man's chart contradicts itself (step 3 closes the right foot just after a right-foot side step, and step 4 is then a left-foot side step), so its feet cannot be matched by a correct conversion; the figure itself is danceable and is kept converted in held_back_figures.

figures.summary: Three right-turning steps where the feet pass instead of closing, like the end of an Open Natural Turn, bringing the man from backing diagonal wall to facing the line of dance.
figures.tip: Count quick-quick-slow and lead with the left side on the last step so the next right step goes outside her; it finishes a Back Lock and leads into a Forward Lock or Natural Turn.

figures.tip: Lower at the end of the quicks before the back step, then rise into the lock; finish it with a Running Finish, Tipple Chasse or Closed Impetus.

figures.name: Double Reverse Spin
figures.summary: A left-turning spin of about seven eighths in six beats: the man turns on his right foot with the left brushed in without weight while the lady does a heel turn and crosses.
figures.tip: Keep the man's left foot light and closed while he turns on the right toe; dance it after a Natural Turn with Hesitation or a Reverse Pivot, and repeat it if you like.

variants.title: Double Reverse Spin

figures.name: Cross Chasse

figures.tip: Keep it straight to diagonal wall and close firmly on the second quick; follow with a Forward Lock, Natural Turn or Quarter Turn to Right taken outside her.

figures.name: Change of Direction
figures.summary: Three slow steps that turn a quarter to the left, the man brushing his left foot in without weight to swing from diagonal wall to diagonal centre.
figures.tip: Stay down with no rise and let the right side lead on the second step; then dance a Chasse Reverse Turn, Progressive Chasse to Right or Cross Chasse.

figures.tip: Turn three eighths before the side step and let her pass outside on the last quick; continue with a Progressive Chasse or Reverse Pivot.

figures.tip: Keep her in front of you through the pivots and use the slows to settle; finish with a Forward Lock or Natural Turn.

figures.name: Closed Telemark
figures.summary: A reverse turn of three quarters in three slows where the lady turns on her heel, ending pointing diagonal wall.
figures.tip: Let her close her feet for the heel turn and finish your third step slightly forward; it leads into a Natural Turn, Forward Lock or Running Finish.

figures.name: Cross Swivel
figures.summary: A gold figure turning a quarter left on one swivel: forward on the left, the right drawn in without weight, then a checked step forward outside partner.
figures.tip: Keep the hips level with no rise and swivel on the ball of the left foot; afterwards go back into a Running Finish or Underturned Tipple Chasse.

followed_by.condition: Running Finish turned 1/4 to end with man facing diagonal wall

figures.name: Six Quick Run
figures.summary: Six quick steps: a back step turning left, a step outside partner and a forward lock, all on quicks for a burst of speed.
figures.tip: Rise at the end of the step before and stay up throughout; enter from a Natural Spin Turn or Closed Impetus and continue with a Forward Lock or Natural Turn.

figures.name: Rumba Cross

figures.tip: Make the first step long and the cross tight, then pivot with the right foot held forward; it is joined to a Natural Pivot Turn by an extra right-foot step.

figures.tip: Count quick-and-quick with small steps and a sudden drop on the last count; use it between a locking figure and a Back Lock or V6.

figures.name: Hover Corte
figures.summary: A gold figure from backing the line of dance: back, side with a hover while turning left, then a weight change back onto the right foot.
figures.tip: Stretch up on the side step and let the body keep turning before the weight change; it follows a Natural Spin Turn, Quarter Turn to Right or Closed Impetus.

std_viennese.name: Viennese Waltz
std_viennese.music: Quick, lilting three-beat music at about sixty bars a minute, classically the Strauss repertoire, with a clear stress on the first beat of every bar.
std_viennese.movement_tip: Let the rotation and the travel come from swinging bodies, not from the feet: keep the steps compact, lower on each first beat and let the turn carry you down the room.
std_viennese.position_tip: Hold a firm, compact closed frame, slightly offset so each partner's right side is in line with the other's centre; the turns only work if your bodies stay connected.

figures.name: Closed Changes
figures.summary: Three-step linking figures that switch the couple from turning right to turning left and back, so Natural and Reverse Turns can alternate.
figures.tip: Use the right-foot change after a Natural Turn to set up a Reverse Turn, Reverse Fleckerl or Contra Check, and the left-foot change after Reverse Turns to return to Natural Turns or a Natural Fleckerl. Think of it as a run straight down the room, not a pause.

figures.name: Natural Turn
figures.summary: The basic right-turning rotation of the Viennese Waltz: six steps and one complete turn while the couple keeps moving along the room.
figures.tip: Repeat it as often as you like, then dance the right-foot Closed Change to switch into Reverse Turns, or go into a Natural Fleckerl. It is the friendlier turn for corners because you can turn it a little less.

followed_by.name: Closed Changes Back - Natural to Reverse

preceded_by.name: Closed Changes Back - Reverse to Natural

figures.name: Reverse Turn
figures.summary: The left-turning rotation: six steps and a full turn travelling along the room, with each partner crossing one foot in front during their forward half.
figures.tip: Place the side step a little behind you so the crossing foot has room. Follow it with the left-foot Closed Change into Natural Turns, or with a Reverse Fleckerl or Contra Check.

followed_by.name: Closed Changes Back - Reverse to Natural

preceded_by.name: Closed Changes Back - Natural to Reverse

figures.name: Closed Changes Backward
figures.summary: Backward versions of the Closed Changes, started with the man moving back after half a turn, so the couple can switch rotation from the other side of the turn.
figures.tip: Dance it straight after steps 1-3 of a Natural Turn (or of a Reverse Turn for the second one) and finish with steps 4-6 of the opposite turn or another backward change. Take a real back step so she has room to travel.

figures.name: Natural Fleckerl
figures.summary: A Gold rotation to the right danced almost on the spot, usually in the middle of the floor, with quick small steps and a crossed foot behind.
figures.tip: Enter from a left-foot Closed Change, a Natural Turn or a Contra Check, and leave into Natural Turns or another Fleckerl. Keep the feet under the body and use part weight on the crossing step so the rotation never stalls.

variants.title: Natural Fleckerl
variants.reason: Re-tried step for step as one foot per count (R L R L R L, half a turn per beat, her feet as charted). The engine rejects it: her body ends up 0.66 to 0.85 m from her standing foot at the cross and untwist steps, whatever way the turn is split between the counts, and her side steps exceed the 0.7 m limit. The untwist rows (turn on one foot, then weight onto the other on the same count) also cannot be written as separate steps.

figures.name: Reverse Fleckerl
figures.summary: The left-turning spot rotation in Gold, with the feet crossing in front and behind while the couple turns around a shared axis.
figures.tip: Start it after a Reverse Turn or the right-foot Closed Change and finish into Reverse Turns, another Fleckerl or a Contra Check. Soft knees and tiny steps keep it compact.

variants.title: Reverse Fleckerl
variants.reason: Re-tried step for step as one foot per count (R L R L R L, half a turn per beat, her feet as charted). The engine rejects it: her body ends up 0.66 to 0.85 m from her standing foot at the cross and untwist steps, whatever way the turn is split between the counts, and her side steps exceed the 0.7 m limit. The untwist rows (turn on one foot, then weight onto the other on the same count) also cannot be written as separate steps.

figures.name: Contra Check
figures.summary: A checking figure that stops the left-turning rotation with a small forward check, rocks back and pivots to the right, so right-turning figures can follow.
figures.tip: Dance it after Reverse Turns, a Reverse Fleckerl or the right-foot Closed Change and continue with a Natural Turn or Natural Fleckerl. Lower into the check and keep the step short.

waltz.name: American Style Waltz
waltz.music: Medium-tempo Latin music with a slow, sensual pulse and a clear beat to settle each step on.
waltz.movement_tip: Keep a soft Cuban motion: the hips settle sideways as each step takes weight, and the knee bends and straightens smoothly. Travel on the ball of the foot and let the heel lower as you take the weight.
waltz.position_tip: Closed hold is relaxed and close, and open facing with one or two hands is just as common. Promenade and side-by-side shapes appear in walks, crossovers and spot turns.

figures.name: Left Box (Reverse) Turn
figures.summary: The classic first waltz figure: a six-step box that can be danced on the spot or with a left turn. It is the usual starting point for new dancers.
figures.tip: Start each half with a soft knee and rise through counts 2 and 3. Follow it with the closed changes, a twinkle or the left cross turn, and do it again to travel round a corner.

figures.name: Hesitations
figures.summary: A hesitation holds the dance for a full bar after a single step. It comes forward and back, or sideways to either side, and it is the simplest way to add a breath to a waltz.
figures.tip: Use the pause to lift up through the rib cage, not to freeze. Dance a forward-and-back hesitation straight after a left box turn, and pick the side version before whisks or a promenade.

figures.name: Cross-Body Lead
figures.summary: The cross-body lead is a three-step change in which the lady crosses in front of the leader. The open version ends with the couple facing each other without contact.
figures.tip: Prepare with a back change or a six-count underarm turn, and clear your own line quickly after step two. It leads on to left boxes, forward changes, twinkles and a left cross turn.

figures.name: Twinkle
figures.summary: The basic twinkle: a forward change that opens into promenade, followed by a crossing step and a side-close that returns to closed hold.
figures.tip: Make the first half a gentle sweep and the second a clear return. It comes after a left box turn, forward changes or a cross-body lead, and you can continue with a promenade chasse.

figures.name: Back Twinkle

figures.tip: Reach back along the diagonal without leaning. It follows a left box turn, backward changes or a cross-body lead, and it can go on to a promenade chasse.

figures.name: Left Cross Turn

figures.summary: Silver-level figures are travelling steps where the feet pass instead of closing. The feather step walks three steps with the last one outside partner, and the three step is a plain forward walk.
figures.tip: Keep the steps a similar size and let the knees do the rising and lowering. Link them with the passing changes or an open turn; they also sit well in front of a box turn.

figures.tip: Keep a firm frame so she can step outside you on the third and sixth steps. It follows a left box or a feather step and leads into a feather step or another open turn.

figures.name: Syncopated Underarm Turns
figures.summary: A quick underarm turn to the right in waltz: the leader steps in a side-close-side pattern while the lady turns right under his raised left hand. It can be danced from outside partner or from open counter promenade.
figures.tip: Raise the hand on the step before she turns and keep your own steps small. The closed version follows passing changes or a feather step, and either version leads on to a feather step or forward changes.

Underarm turn to R. from Open CPP

figures.name: Twinkles to PP and CPP
figures.summary: A silver chain of twinkles that passes through promenade and counter promenade, with brushes in place of the bronze closes and a finishing step outside partner.
figures.tip: Brush the free foot smoothly and keep your head lines clear as the direction swaps. It follows a left box or passing changes, and ends into an open turn or a feather step. The progressive version has footing typos in the lady's chart on the site.

variants.title: Progressive Twinkles to PP and CPP
variants.reason: the site's lady's chart puts steps 3 and 6 on the wrong foot (typos), so no legal foot sequence can match it

figures.name: Promenade & Counter Promenade Runs
figures.summary: Silver runs that swap between promenade and counter promenade, either to the right (natural), to the left (reverse), or with a turn for the lady in the middle bar.
figures.tip: Let the shoulders and head set each new line, and keep the travel steady. The runs follow twinkles or a left box, and lead on to a feather step; the lady's-turn version is danced after the natural runs.

variants.title: PP & CPP Runs w/ Lady's Turn

figures.name: Promenade Release
figures.summary: A promenade release in which one partner circles around the other: the lady walks round the leader, or the leader walks round the lady, before both end in open counter promenade.
figures.tip: Keep an open frame and extend the arm so the traveller has room. It follows a whisk or a twinkle into promenade, and it leads to a closing twinkle or a syncopated underarm turn.

figures.name: Underarm Release
figures.summary: An underarm release lets the lady turn away under the leader's arm and out of closed hold. The site gives no steps for it.
figures.tip: Because the site charts nothing for it, treat it as a link idea only: lift the hand early and pair it with the closing twinkle or an open turn.

variants.title: Underarm Release
variants.reason: the site gives no man's or lady's chart for this figure

figures.name: Closing Twinkle
figures.summary: A closing twinkle that brings the couple from open counter promenade back into closed hold: either the lady passes round the leader or the leader circles round the lady, then both finish through promenade.
figures.tip: Keep the frame lifted during the pass so the closed hold is easy to take. It follows a promenade release or a syncopated underarm turn and leads on to a feather step or box.

figures.name: Outside Check & Develope
figures.summary: A check and a leg extension: the leader checks forward outside partner, holds through two counts while the lady lifts and extends her free leg, then both finish with a turning continuity step. It can be danced on either side of her.
figures.tip: Keep your supporting knee soft and use a slight rise to lead her develope. It follows a feather step or passing changes and leads on to a feather step or an open turn.

variants.title: Outside Check & Develope in RSP
variants.reason: the site's man's chart says to check weight on the left foot while stepping forward on the right (a typo), so no legal foot sequence can match it

figures.name: Wing
figures.summary: A short promenade figure in which the leader steps through and closes without weight while the lady walks forward round him into left side position.
figures.tip: Keep your own weight over the right foot and let the body turn lead her. Follow a twinkle or a promenade figure and continue with a closing twinkle or feather step.

figures.name: Weave
figures.summary: A continuous left-turning figure of two bars, in which the leader alternates stepping outside partner while turning to the left. It travels down the line of dance.
figures.tip: Keep a firm frame and let the body carry the turn through both bars. It follows a feather step or an open turn and goes on to a feather step or passing changes.

figures.name: Natural Pivots
figures.summary: A pivoting figure danced from promenade: the leader alternates stepping forward and pivoting back, turning to the right through nearly two full turns before returning to promenade.
figures.tip: Keep your head still and let the body rotate over the supporting foot. It follows a twinkle or a promenade chasse and goes on to a chasse, a hover corte or a wing.

figures.name: Slip Pivot
figures.summary: A pivoting figure in which the leader slips back in fallaway and pivots to the left. It can be danced from closed hold or after a check in promenade.
figures.tip: Slip the feet back lightly and turn from the body, not the arms. The closed version follows a left cross turn or twinkle, and either version leads on to a feather step or box.

figures.name: Fallaway Lock
figures.summary: The fallaway lock closes a side-by-side pattern: the leader takes three steps beside the lady, then turns and releases her into a free turn or an underarm turn ending in open position or counter promenade.
figures.tip: Start from the left side-by-side hold and lead the lady's turn with a lifted left arm; follow it with a feather step or a twinkle. All three of the site's lady's charts have footing typos.

variants.title: Free Turn ending
variants.reason: the site's lady's chart puts steps 5 and 6 on the same foot (a typo), and the figure starts side by side, so no legal foot sequence can match it

variants.title: Underarm Turn ending to OP
variants.reason: the site's lady's chart puts steps 2 and 3 on the same foot (a typo), and the figure starts side by side, so no legal foot sequence can match it

variants.title: Underarm Turn ending to CPP
variants.reason: the site's lady's chart puts steps 2 and 3 on the same foot (a typo), and the figure starts side by side, so no legal foot sequence can match it

figures.name: Criss Cross Changes
figures.summary: A criss-cross sequence for open position in which the lady passes back and forth under the leader's raised left hand while he steps across and behind her.
figures.tip: Keep the hand level and the arm lifted so she can cross comfortably, and dance your own steps compactly. It follows a promenade release or closing twinkle and leads on to another open figure.

figures.name: Waltz Variation 1
figures.summary: A long gold routine that begins with a left box half, a slip pivot and a rock into promenade, releases the lady into side-by-side chasses with a check, and then returns through her left underarm turn to a promenade chasse.
figures.tip: Learn it in phrases: box and pivot, rock to promenade, side-by-side chasse and check, underarm turn, promenade chasse and close. It is danced around a corner, so start facing line of dance near it.

figures.name: Waltz Variation 2
figures.summary: A gold routine that opens with a twinkle and an open natural turn, adds a tipple chasse into pivots with a ronde, a slip pivot, an open reverse turn and whisk, and ends with a twist turn in which the lady runs round the leader.
figures.tip: Work through it in blocks: twinkle and open natural turn, tipple chasse and pivots, check and ronde, slip pivot, open reverse and whisk, twist turn, then the promenade chasse and close. Keep the twist turn quiet and let her run round you.

variants.title: Waltz Variation 2
variants.reason: the chart runs 36 beats (twelve bars), over the game's limit of 32 beats for one figure

figures.name: Waltz Variation 3
figures.summary: A gold routine that starts with a twinkle and a spin through promenade into side-by-side position, then dances side-by-side changes, a fallaway turn, two underarm turns, an outside check with a develope, and a left box turn to finish.
figures.tip: Learn the three underarm turns as separate phrases first, then link them with the side-by-side changes. The check and develope needs a firm standing leg and the left box turn gets you back into closed hold.

variants.title: Waltz Variation 3
variants.reason: the chart runs well over 32 beats (about thirteen bars), over the game's limit of 32 beats for one figure

figures.name: Waltz Variation 4
figures.summary: A gold routine that turns the lady into shadow position, dances turning runs and a pivot in shadow, then slides back into closed hold for a swivel, a hold in the pose, a pass round the lady and a promenade finish.
figures.tip: Keep the contact steady when you change from closed to shadow and back, and let her turn lead you. Rehearse the shadow section with a partner before adding the first four bars.

variants.title: Waltz Variation 4
variants.reason: the chart is danced partly in shadow position and runs 39 beats, which the game's holds and 32-beat figure limit cannot represent

figures.name: Waltz Variation 5
figures.summary: A gold routine that opens with a promenade and an underarm pass, adds side-cross-replace whisks as the lady circles behind the leader, and then travels in eight circling runs before a whisk and a closing move.
figures.tip: Keep the circling runs small and lift your frame so she can travel round with you. The pass and whisks come first, so settle the early bars, then add the runs and the finishing whisk.

tango.name: American Style Tango
tango.music: Medium-tempo orchestral tango with a firm, sometimes march-like beat that invites sharp, clean steps.
tango.movement_tip: Pick the feet up and place them with a cat-like, stalking action rather than gliding, and keep the body level with no rise and fall. Walks bend gently to the left, so plan where each figure will point you.
tango.position_tip: The hold is more compact than a normal ballroom hold: she stands further to his right, his right hand reaches around her back, and her left forearm slips under his arm. Keep the elbows a little higher and the frame quiet.

figures.name: The Tango Close
figures.summary: The cadence that finishes most Bronze and Silver figures: three steps in quick, quick, slow, with the free foot drawn in at the end. It comes in several forms: forward, backward, to promenade, and with a drag or a point.
figures.tip: On the last count bring the free foot in beside the standing foot and keep your weight on the other leg, so the next figure can start on that same free foot. Then link into walks, a corte or a rock.

figures.name: 8-Count Basic
figures.summary: The first Tango figure: a pair of slow walks followed by a quick-quick-slow ending, five steps in eight beats. Drawing the free foot in at the end keeps the same foot ready for the next figure.
figures.tip: Place each walk with a crisp, flexed knee and let the line curve slowly left. Afterwards go into a Basic Corte, Progressive Rocks, an Open Left Turn or a Rock to Promenade.

figures.name: Left Cross Turn
figures.summary: A turning figure in which the man crosses the left foot in front of the right and keeps turning left, while the lady crosses in front on the last step. The version from promenade starts with the lady's side step.
figures.tip: Cross close to the supporting foot and keep your knees flexed so the turn does not drift. Dance it from closed hold and follow it with a basic or any left-foot figure.

figures.name: Promenade Ronde, Slip & Swivel
figures.summary: A promenade figure with a pointing ronde on the fourth step, a fallaway back step and a slip, ending with a forward Tango Close.
figures.tip: Draw the ronde as a smooth half circle on the floor, then keep the back steps small. Start it from promenade and finish with a Basic or other left-foot figure.

variants.title: Promenade Ronde, Slip & Swivel
variants.reason: the site's man's chart gives the right foot for both step 8 and the first step of the closing Tango Close, so the foot sequence cannot be danced as written

figures.name: Natural Turn from Promenade
figures.summary: A right-turning figure from promenade: the pair travel along the line of dance and then turn right, with the lady stepping outside the man. The longer version continues into a quick Tango Close.
figures.tip: Make the turn from the body on step 3 and keep the following steps compact. The turn leaves her outside you, so continue with Outside Swivels or another figure starting back on the left.

variants.title: Natural Turn to Quick Tango Close

figures.name: Cobra Fans
figures.summary: A four-step figure of slow fans: the man steps back and reaches the free leg, then walks forward into promenade, twice. It ends in promenade.
figures.tip: Settle onto the standing leg before each reach and keep the fan low and controlled. Follow it with a promenade figure.

figures.name: Change of Places
figures.summary: A side-by-side figure in which the partners exchange places in six steps, quick, quick, slow twice. A version has the man turning, and another leads to left side position.
figures.tip: Keep the joined hands level and relaxed so they guide the exchange instead of pulling. Reach it from a Release to Side-by-Side or a Right Side Release, and follow with walks or a Tango Close Ending.

variants.title: Change of Places - Man Turning
variants.reason: the site's lady's chart lists only three of the six steps the man dances, so her part cannot be matched step by step

variants.title: Change of Places to Left Side Pos.

figures.name: Right Side Release
figures.summary: A promenade figure that opens up into right side-by-side position in five steps, slow, slow, quick, quick, slow.
figures.tip: Ease the hold open over the last three steps instead of dropping it. After it, the Change of Places to Left Side Position carries on from the same side.

figures.name: Syncopated Underarm Turn to R.
figures.summary: A short underarm turn in which the lady turns right under the man's raised hand, danced in quick, quick, and, slow rhythm. One version starts with her outside him and another from side-by-side.
figures.tip: Raise the hand on the and count and give her a clear path to circle under it. Close hold or a Tango Close Ending can follow, depending on the starting version.

figures.name: Step-Points
figures.summary: Four quick steps in which each partner alternately steps and points the free foot to the side, with either the man or the lady travelling forward.
figures.tip: Keep your weight over the supporting foot and let the point be a light touch. The figure can be used almost anywhere in closed or open hold, for instance after a Basic or as a link.

figures.name: Cross-Body Lead to Underarm Turn L.
figures.summary: A cross-body lead that changes into a left underarm turn for the lady: the man leads her past him, then stands almost still while she turns under his raised hand.
figures.tip: Stay quiet during the hold and keep the raised hand steady above her head. It starts with the right foot back, so it can follow an Overturned Ending, and you can continue with walks in open hold.

variants.title: Cross-Body Lead to Underarm Turn L.

figures.name: Cross Body Lead to X-Line & Swivel
figures.summary: A longer figure of eleven steps: an Open Left Turn into promenade, a pause while the lady swivels, then a forward Tango Close.
figures.tip: Treat the pause as three slow counts of stillness for the man while her swivels do the work. Use it after a Basic and follow it with walks or a rock.

variants.title: Cross Body Lead to X-Line & Swivel

figures.name: Promenade Kick-Ball Change
figures.summary: A Closed Promenade with an extra kick and a quick change of weight after the second step.
figures.tip: Keep the kick small and from the knee and take the weight change on the and count. It starts from promenade and finishes like the Closed Promenade.

figures.name: Promenade Fan Swivel
figures.summary: A Closed Promenade with a closing action and quick change of weight inserted after the step across.
figures.tip: Close the foot lightly, then change weight on the and so the finish stays on rhythm. Dance it from promenade and follow with a basic or rock.

figures.name: Promenade Lock
figures.summary: A promenade figure with a quick lock step in the middle, travelling along the line of dance and staying in promenade.
figures.tip: Keep the locking foot close and the steps small so the pair travels smoothly. Combine it with other promenade figures, such as the Closed Promenade or Natural Turn from Promenade.

figures.name: Slip Pivot
figures.summary: A three-step figure in which the man steps back in fallaway and then pivots, while the lady slips her foot back and pivots forward on the last quick.
figures.tip: Begin with the right foot back, so dance it after an Overturned Ending, and keep your frame still as the pivot turns the pair. Follow with a Basic or any left-foot figure.

variants.title: Slip Pivot
variants.reason: in fallaway position both partners step backward at once, which the game's closed hold cannot show, since it keeps her facing him and moving the opposite way

figures.name: Corte Roll-In / Roll-Out
figures.summary: A Basic Corte preceded by two linked dips: back and forward corte actions, each with a replacement and a close, in a sixteen-beat phrase.
figures.tip: Sink into the standing knee on each check and recover with a soft replace. Dance it after a Basic or a rock; it ends like the Basic Corte, so any left-foot figure may follow.

figures.name: Shadow Roll-In / Roll-Out
figures.summary: A side-by-side figure in which the man stays on the spot while the lady rolls forward and back in front of him, ending in shadow position.
figures.tip: Stay quiet on the spot and let the lady's movement carry the figure. Start it from a left side-by-side position, with joined hands, and then dance the shadow figures that follow.

variants.title: Shadow Roll-In / Roll-Out
variants.reason: the man takes no steps in this variant and the dancers move in shadow position, which the game's holds cannot show

figures.name: Shadow Basic
figures.summary: The basic walks, two slow and a quick, quick, slow ending, danced in shadow position with the lady in front of the man and offset to his right.
figures.tip: Keep your steps exactly the same as hers so the pair moves as one. It follows the Shadow Roll-In and leads on into the Shadow Rocks.

variants.title: Shadow Basic
variants.reason: the dancers move in shadow position, one behind the other on the same foot, and the game's holds (closed, promenade, open, fan) cannot show that

figures.name: Shadow Rocks
figures.summary: The Progressive Rocks danced in shadow position, with the lady in front of the man and offset to his right, both on the same foot.
figures.tip: Match her timing exactly so the two of you look like one. It sits between shadow figures such as the Shadow Basic and the shadow roll.

variants.title: Shadow Rocks
variants.reason: the dancers move in shadow position, one behind the other on the same foot, and the game's holds (closed, promenade, open, fan) cannot show that

figures.name: Oversway
figures.summary: A dramatic showpiece in which the couple sway together over a side step, hold the picture for a slow, then close and open to promenade.
figures.tip: Stretch the supporting side up and let the sway start from the ribs, not the neck. Because it ends in promenade, a promenade figure such as the Closed Promenade follows well.

figures.name: Tango Variation 1
figures.summary: A 33-step routine that opens with the 8-Count Basic, moves through promenade with brushes and a ronde, and finishes in promenade after several turns of the lady and a brief same-foot position.
figures.tip: Learn it in sections: the promenade opening, the brush walks, then the quick sequence at the end. Keep the brush steps clean and the transition between them smooth, and let the music phrase the whole routine.

variants.title: Tango Variation 1
variants.reason: the lady's chart gives the left foot on three steps in a row (steps 18 to 20), which cannot be danced, step 28 is a same-foot shadow position, and the routine is far longer than the game's 32-beat limit

figures.name: Tango Variation 2
figures.summary: A 35-step routine with a hooked leg, a corte, side-by-side sections and a passage in shadow position, all linked by Tango Walks and promenade steps.
figures.tip: Practise the hooked-leg moment on its own first, and keep the shadow walks tidy, matching the lady's feet exactly. Dance the routine to a full musical phrase and use the Tango Close at the end.

variants.title: Tango Variation 2
variants.reason: steps 22 to 27 are danced in shadow position, one behind the other on the same foot, which the game's holds cannot show

figures.name: Tango Variation 3
figures.summary: A 38-step routine travelling through promenade with kicks, locks and a ronde, then a sequence of pivots in cuddle position ending with a swivel and close.
figures.tip: Give each pattern its own picture: the promenade kicks, the locks, and the cuddle pivots. Keep the steps small in the cuddle sections, and finish with a clear swivel.

variants.title: Tango Variation 3
variants.reason: steps 29 to 32 are danced in cuddle position, with the lady on one side of the man's body in turn, which the game's holds cannot show

figures.name: Tango Variation 4
figures.summary: A 29-step routine of Tango Walks, closes, a roll through promenade and a shadow section with optional fans or flicks, finishing with the basic ending.
figures.tip: Match your timing to your partner's during the shadow section and keep the fans controlled. Work out in advance which optional point you will use and stay consistent through the sequence.

variants.title: Tango Variation 4
variants.reason: steps 19 and 20 are danced in shadow position, with the lady in front on the man's right, which the game's holds cannot show

figures.name: Tango Variation 5
figures.summary: A 29-step routine of walks and many small rocks, a crossing step behind with a quick change of weight, a side-by-side swivel passage and a basic ending.
figures.tip: Keep the rocks tiny and quick so that the travelling steps stand out, and settle the cross behind before the quick change of weight. Dance it to a full musical phrase, starting in closed hold.

variants.title: Tango Variation 5
variants.reason: the routine runs about 40 beats, and the game limits a figure to 32 beats, so it cannot be played as one figure

foxtrot.name: American Style Foxtrot
foxtrot.music: Medium-tempo jazz and swing tunes with a relaxed, walking pulse.
foxtrot.movement_tip: Walk forward heel first and back toe first, letting the feet glide past each other with soft knees. Bronze keeps the rise gentle on the chasse; from Silver a smooth three-step rise and fall and light sway appear.
foxtrot.position_tip: Closed hold with light body contact, a little offset to the left, is the home position. Promenade and open shapes appear as the syllabus grows.

figures.name: Forward Basic
figures.summary: The basic travelling figure of foxtrot: two long walks and a side-close chasse. It can be repeated down the line of dance.
figures.tip: Roll through each walk heel first, then lower on the chasse. Chain it with itself, a Back Basic, a Promenade or any turn figure, since nearly everything in Bronze can follow it.

figures.name: Back Basic
figures.summary: The reverse of the Forward Basic: two backward walks and a chasse, taking the man against the line of dance.
figures.tip: Keep your head over your standing foot while the other foot reaches back. Use it straight after a Forward Basic to make a back-and-forth pattern on a short wall.

figures.name: Hesitation Left Turn
figures.summary: A forward hesitation followed by the second half of a left box turn. It is a quick way to turn the corner to the left.
figures.tip: Keep the first slow straight and start the body turn only as you rock back. Dance it after a Forward Basic and follow with another basic to go on round the room.

figures.name: Hesitation Right Turn
figures.summary: Step back and pause, then start a right-hand turn: the easiest way to turn right in Bronze.
figures.tip: Stay still on step 1 and let your right side lead into the turn. It joins well after a Back Basic and into a Right Pivot Turn or Promenade figures.

figures.name: Left Box (Reverse) Turn
figures.summary: An alternative basic made of two chasse halves, a forward one and a backward one, turning left.
figures.tip: Keep the turn even across both halves so you finish square to the wall. It can go into a basic, a hesitation or a Right Box Turn, so use it to turn a corner.

figures.name: Side Sway
figures.summary: A playful alternative to the basic, entirely sideways in slow-slow-quick-quick.
figures.tip: Brush the free foot in before each slow and keep the frame still. Dance it between basics to use time on a short wall.

figures.name: Promenade
figures.summary: The classic way to open into promenade position and close again: a side step, a walk across and a chasse.
figures.tip: Keep your head turned to the line of travel while in promenade and close fully on the chasse. Follow it with a Forward Basic or Back Basic depending on who turns to whom, or with another Promenade.

figures.tip: Treat step 5 as one tidy pivot with the weight over the standing foot; do not hop. It follows a Hesitation Right Turn or a forward basic and leads into another basic or a Hesitation Right Turn.

figures.name: Twinkle
figures.summary: The most-used foxtrot figure: a forward slow, a chasse to promenade, a promenade walk and a chasse back to closed.
figures.tip: Make the first chasse small and open the frame to the line of travel; then walk across and square off. It follows turn figures such as the Left Box or Hesitation and leads to the Promenade Check, Twist Turn or Pivot as well as any basic.

figures.name: Back Twinkle
figures.summary: The backward version of the twinkle, opening into promenade after a first backward slow.
figures.tip: Reach the first back step with the toe and keep your head up toward her. Use it after a Left Box, a Hesitation Left Turn or a Promenade, and follow it with any basic.

figures.name: Twinkles to PP & CPP
figures.summary: Three twinkles in a row: the couple moves from promenade to counter promenade and back, then closes. The progressive variant starts with a small left turn and travels straight.
figures.tip: Make the changes of side crisp: cross on each slow, chasse softly on the quicks. Come into it from a Hesitation Right Turn, and follow it with any basic.

figures.name: Promenade Check
figures.summary: A promenade in which the second walk is checked, then the weight returns. It can stay in promenade, turn into a Back Basic, or end in a slip pivot.
figures.tip: Flex the knee gently on the check; do not stop dead. It arrives from a Hesitation Right Turn or a Left Box, and the Back Basic and slip pivot variants flow straight into more turns.

figures.name: Promenade Twist Turn
figures.summary: A promenade whose second step crosses in front and unwinds into a half turn to the left, also called a corkscrew.
figures.tip: Stay tall on the ball of the foot while the feet untwist. Dance it after a Hesitation Right Turn or a Left Box, then continue with any basic or turn.

figures.name: Promenade Pivot
figures.summary: A pivot dance from promenade: the man pivots to the right while the lady circles round him into closed hold.
figures.tip: Keep your free foot close to the standing foot for the pivot and let her travel around you. Arrive from a Promenade or a Left Box and finish into any basic.

figures.name: Grapevines
figures.summary: A zig-zag figure: a short basic start followed by forward, side, back, side steps with a small turn to each side.
figures.tip: Keep the angles gentle and each step the same size. It follows a Hesitation Left Turn or a Left Box and ends ready for a basic or Twinkle.

figures.name: Continuity Runs
figures.summary: A run of continuous passing steps in slow-quick-quick time, travelling forward along the line of dance without closing the feet.
figures.tip: Keep the feet passing smoothly and let each quick stay small. Use it after a Twinkle or Passing Change, and finish it into a basic or a Twinkle so the chain of steps does not run out.

variants.title: Continuity Runs
variants.reason: the site's chart page returned an error

figures.name: Open Reverse Turn
figures.summary: A six-step left-turning figure with a back step outside partner in the middle, the first of the Silver 'open' turns.
figures.tip: Keep your left side leading and spread the turn through all six steps. It follows a Hesitation or Left Box and leads into the Passing Changes, a Twinkle or an Open Natural Turn.

figures.name: Open Natural Turn
figures.summary: The right-turning companion of the Open Reverse Turn: six continuous steps starting on the right foot.
figures.tip: Plan the foot: it starts on the right and ends on the left. Dance it from a figure ending with weight on the left foot, then pass outside her on the next step.

figures.name: Brush Twinkle
figures.summary: The Silver twinkle: it keeps the promenade shape of the Bronze Twinkle but replaces the closes with brushes so the feet keep passing.
figures.tip: Brush lightly rather than close, and keep the weight rolling forward. It arrives after an Open Reverse Turn or Twinkle, and goes on to any figure that begins with the left foot.

figures.name: Back Twinkle
figures.summary: The back twinkle of Silver, in three versions: the plain one steps diagonally back, the natural one heel-turns to the right, and the reverse one turns left into promenade.
figures.tip: Whichever you pick, travel back for the first two steps and then open to promenade on the third. Link them from a Left Box or Hesitation and follow with any left-foot figure.

figures.name: Hover Corte
figures.summary: A short three-step figure in which the dancer hovers over a step: the weight goes out, then back, producing a hesitation and a change of direction.
figures.tip: Take the second step lightly and stay tall so the replace feels like a lift. It follows a Twinkle or turn from closed, and the promenade variant follows a promenade ending.

variants.title: Hover Corte
variants.reason: the lady's chart repeats the right foot on steps 2 and 3, a contradiction the game cannot dance; the promenade version is playable

figures.name: Passing Changes Forward
figures.summary: A chain of forward passing steps with brushes and small turns, in slow-quick-quick time, plus a short three-step version.
figures.tip: Keep your steps flat and continuous, with no closing between them. Start from an Open Reverse Turn or Twinkle and end into a Hesitation or a Left Box; the narrow change joins two longer figures.

figures.name: Passing Changes Back
figures.summary: Passing changes travelling backward: an open reverse start followed by three backward groups with brushes and small turns.
figures.tip: Stay close in the frame and use your left side to steer the turns. It follows a Left Box or Hesitation Left Turn, and leaves into a basic or a Hesitation.

figures.name: Twinkles to PP & CPP
figures.summary: The Silver version of the three-twinkle chain: brushes replace closes, hold changes from promenade to counter promenade and back, and the lady turns round the leader. The progressive variant has the same footwork with less turn.
figures.tip: Make each change of side crisp and let the lady's turn do the travelling; keep your own turn small. Arrive from an Open Reverse Turn or Brush Twinkle and leave through any left-foot figure.

figures.name: Promenade & Counter-Promenade Runs
figures.summary: Runs that travel along the line of dance through promenade and counter promenade, with the leader turning either right or left and the lady passing in front of him. A short variant lets the lady spin on her own.
figures.tip: Make the runs flow without stopping, and keep the arms firm enough for her to find the hold changes. They start after a Twinkle or Brush Twinkle and finish with the normal twinkle closing steps.

variants.title: PP & CPP Runs w/ Lady's Turn

figures.name: Syncopated Underarm Turns
figures.summary: A syncopated underarm turn: slow, quick, and, quick, in which the lady turns once to the right under the leader's raised left hand. It can be danced from closed or from open counter promenade.
figures.tip: Count it slow, quick-and-quick and keep the hand circle smooth and early. It follows an Open Reverse Turn or twinkle from closed, or a Promenade Release from open counter promenade, and leads on to any left-foot figure.

variants.title: Syncopated Underarm Turn to R. from O.P.
Syncopated Underarm Turn to R. from Open CPP

figures.name: Promenade Release
figures.summary: A hold change from promenade to open counter promenade: either the lady circles in front of the man, or he circles in front of her.
figures.tip: Keep the left-hand connection light and let the circling partner finish square to the line of travel. It follows a Twinkle to promenade, and leads into the Underarm Release or Closing Twinkle.

figures.name: Underarm Release
figures.summary: A hold change from promenade to open counter promenade in which one partner passes underneath the raised joined hands: the lady in one variant, the man in the other.
figures.tip: Raise the joined hand early and keep it steady so the partner can pass without ducking. Dance it after a promenade twinkle and follow with a Closing Twinkle.

figures.name: Closing Twinkle
figures.summary: The closing twinkle of Silver: from open counter promenade one partner closes round the other, and the couple finishes with promenade and a closing side step.
figures.tip: Pass round your partner in a close curve and take closed hold before the promenade. It follows a Promenade Release or Underarm Release and leads into any left-foot figure.

figures.name: Curved Feathers
figures.summary: A curving feather-style figure for Full Silver: forward steps outside partner that bend smoothly along the line of dance.
figures.tip: Let the curve come from the body turn rather than from twisting the feet, and keep each step long and flowing. Connect it to the other Silver continuity figures such as passing changes and the open turns.

variants.title: Curved Feathers
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Curved Threes
figures.summary: A curving three-step figure for Full Silver, travelling forward through a gentle turn.
figures.tip: Keep the three steps even and let the turn grow gradually. Use it as a connector between the open turns and the promenade figures.

variants.title: Curved Threes
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Grapevines
figures.summary: Eight quick steps that zig-zag down the room: forward, side, back, side, repeated twice. One version starts on the right foot and goes left, the other starts on the left and goes right.
figures.tip: Keep every quick the same size and let the turn come from your body. The first one starts on the right foot, so use it after an Open Natural Turn or Narrow Passing Change; the second follows a left-foot ending.

variants.title: Grapevines to Left
variants.reason: the man's chart lists the left foot on steps 2, 3 and 4, which cannot be danced; it is the mirror of the playable version to the right

figures.name: Promenade Grapevines
figures.summary: Four quick steps in promenade that close briefly into hold, step back across in a fallaway shape and open to promenade again.
figures.tip: Think of a small closed-hold moment on the second step, then open again; keep the steps light and even. It repeats on itself and links to Natural Pivots or a Hover Corte.

figures.name: Open Counter-Promenade Grapevines
figures.summary: Four quick steps in open counter promenade: forward, side, back across and side, with the couple turning to face and then returning to the original shape.
figures.tip: Use small, light steps and keep the connection gentle. It follows a Promenade Release or Syncopated Underarm Turn and leads on to a Closing Twinkle.

figures.name: Step-Points
figures.summary: Four quick steps made of two step-and-point actions, danced with the man going forward or the lady going forward.
figures.tip: Keep the point light and the standing knee soft, turning a quarter on each foot. Dance it after a Twinkle or Open Turn, or between two Grapevines.

figures.name: Natural Pivots
figures.summary: A figure of continuous pivots from promenade: the man and lady rotate around each other along the line of dance and return to promenade.
figures.tip: Keep the pivot foot light and the body tall, and let the turn keep going between steps. It follows Promenade Grapevines or a similar promenade ending and can repeat itself.

figures.name: Foxtrot Variation 1
figures.summary: A 26-step gold routine that combines twinkles and runs in handshake hold, an underarm turn for the lady, a change of places into a cuddle shape with a supported lunge, and a free spin before returning to closed hold.
figures.tip: Break it into its parts and learn the handshake runs and the lady's turns first. The cuddle and lunge need a trusting partner and a strong standing leg, so practise them slowly before you add the music.

variants.title: Foxtrot Variation 1
variants.reason: the chart includes a cuddle position with the lady behind the man and a supported lunge in which she falls onto him, which the game's holds cannot show

figures.name: Foxtrot Variation 2
figures.summary: A 32-step gold routine built from familiar figures: a curved three step, a checked back run, swivels, passing changes, grapevines both ways, an underarm turn for the lady, a promenade step and a left box finish.
figures.tip: Learn it in blocks of eight steps and name each block as you dance it. The lady's underarm turn on the last quicks of the grapevines is the tricky moment, so lift the left hand early and keep it steady.

variants.title: Foxtrot Variation 2
variants.reason: the routine runs 40 beats (ten bars), longer than the 32-beat limit for one game figure

figures.name: Foxtrot Variation 3
figures.summary: A 34-step gold routine with twinkle and grapevine patterns, a twist in which the man unwinds under his own raised arm, a free turn for the lady into shadow position, step-point zig-zags, a pivot sequence and a promenade finish.
figures.tip: Master the twist and untwist on its own first, with the weight shared between the ball of one foot and the heel of the other. Then add the shadow position and the repeated step-points.

variants.title: Foxtrot Variation 3
variants.reason: the chart includes shadow position, in which the lady stands directly in front of or beside the man facing the same way, which the game's holds cannot show

figures.name: Foxtrot Variation 4
figures.summary: The fourth gold variation, a long routine combining the foxtrot figures of the Silver syllabus into one sequence.
figures.tip: Choose figures you can lead cleanly and join them with Twinkles and Passing Changes, keeping each hold change clear. Practise the connections between the figures as much as the figures themselves.

variants.title: Foxtrot Variation 4
variants.reason: the site's chart page returned an error

figures.name: Foxtrot Variation 5
figures.summary: The fifth gold variation, a long routine that links several foxtrot figures into one choreographed sequence.
figures.tip: Build it one phrase at a time and check that each figure ends on the foot the next one needs. Repeat the hardest connection slowly before dancing the whole routine to music.

variants.title: Foxtrot Variation 5
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

chacha.name: Cha Cha
chacha.music: Medium-tempo Latin music with a steady, punchy beat and a strong accent on the first count.
chacha.movement_tip: Keep the weighted leg straight and let the hips settle toward it; take each step with the ball of the foot first and lower the heel as weight arrives.
chacha.position_tip: Stand tall with weight forward over the balls of the feet, hold a compact frame, and keep a soft, connected clasp through the raised hands.

figures.name: Closed Basic Movement
figures.summary: The foundation of the dance: a forward or back break, then a side chasse, danced in closed hold and alternating between the two halves.
figures.tip: Keep the breaks compact and the chasse small; the basic joins naturally to the Fan, Underarm Turns, Spot Turns and the New York, and can be repeated as long as you like.

figures.summary: A turn under the arm to the right, usually started from fan position, in which she walks a wide triangle and finishes facing him.
figures.tip: Let her walk up to your side before you raise the hand; it follows the Fan and flows into a basic, Natural Top or opening out.

figures.name: Hockey Stick
figures.summary: A progressive turn under the arm to the left, begun in fan position, with a hockey-stick-shaped track for the lady.
figures.tip: Cross behind on the Cuban cross and keep the left hand raised until she has finished turning; it follows a Fan and leads to an Open Basic, Shoulder to Shoulder or Time Steps.
