figures.name: Natural Top
figures.summary: A closed-hold spinning pattern in which the couple circles about a point between them, alternating side steps and crosses behind.
figures.tip: Keep the steps tiny and rotate evenly around the shared centre; finish on any first count and lead into a basic or opening out.

figures.name: Natural Opening Out Movement
figures.summary: A break danced in right side position, with her stepping back, followed by a chasse that returns her to closed hold.
figures.tip: Offset your body slightly right to start, then rotate left on the chasse; it is a standard ending to the Alemana or the Natural Top.

followed_by.name: Open Basic Movement
followed_by.condition: Open Basic Movement commencing in closed position.

figures.name: Closed Hip Twist
figures.summary: A two-bar figure that begins like the opening out and ends in fan position, with a twisting action for the lady.
figures.tip: Keep her close through the first bar and release the right hand only in the second; it follows an Alemana or Natural Top and leads to an Alemana or Hockey Stick.

figures.name: Open Hip Twist
figures.summary: A hip twist danced from open position in which he draws his left arm back so she twists forward into fan.
figures.tip: Draw the left hand toward your hip rather than pulling her; follow it with an Alemana or Hockey Stick from the fan.

figures.name: Reverse Top
figures.summary: A reverse spin in closed hold: step aside on the right and swivel left crossing the left in front, repeated to spin left.
figures.tip: Keep the steps small and the swivel on the ball of the foot; end on the first count of a bar and continue with an opening out.

figures.name: Opening Out from Reverse Top
figures.summary: A short exit from the Reverse Top: two steps with the Cuban cross, then a chasse that sends her out into fan.
figures.tip: Release the right hand on the Cuban cross and extend the left arm gently; it is the exit from the Reverse Top into fan.

variants.title: Opening Out from Reverse Top
variants.reason: The site's lady chart gives only three rows for a five-step chasse (the range is mistyped), so the literal step count cannot match his five steps.

figures.name: Aida
figures.summary: A backward pattern from closed hold: both partners step back and turn slightly away from each other, finishing side by side after a back lock.
figures.tip: Release the right hand on the first step, keep the left arm toned, and match her back steps so you stay level.

variants.title: Aida
variants.reason: The site's man chart gives three rows for a five-step back lock (mistyped range) while her chart gives five, so the literal step counts cannot match.

figures.name: Spiral
figures.summary: A hip-twist family figure where the lady performs a spiral turn under his raised hand and finishes in fan position.
figures.tip: Raise the hand over her head only on the chasse and keep her moving forward; it ends in fan, so follow with an Alemana or Hockey Stick.

figures.name: Curl
figures.summary: A variation that starts from open position with a circling hand and then finishes with the second bar of the Spiral.
figures.tip: Start the hand circle as she steps across; this leads into fan, so follow with an Alemana or Hockey Stick.

figures.name: Rope Spinning
figures.summary: The lady spins quickly off his raised hand, then circles him with forward locks while he dances small chasses and circles his hand overhead.
figures.tip: Give her room with a clear lead and keep your own steps small; it can follow the figure before it without a prep and finish in closed or open hold.

figures.name: Cross Basic
figures.summary: A basic in which the first step of each bar is a cross, turning gently left through two bars.
figures.tip: Keep a soft cross with the toe turned out and travel little; it follows a basic and flows back into one.

figures.name: Cuban Breaks
figures.summary: Tiny, quick cross-and-replace steps, danced with half-beat timing, in which the partners angle slightly away from each other.
figures.tip: Keep the steps small and the body angle subtle; it sits between a basic and any next figure and works best as a short accent.

figures.name: Chase
figures.summary: An open, no-hold figure in which the partners turn in tandem, one chasing the other with forward locks over four bars.
figures.tip: Practise the half turns on the spot first and keep strict eye contact; it is a showy pattern for the end of a routine.

variants.title: Chase
variants.reason: Danced in open position with no hold, partners in tandem and apart for four bars, which the game's holds cannot show faithfully.

figures.name: Advanced Hip Twist
figures.summary: A more advanced hip twist, in which the lady's turn is extended before she finishes in fan.
figures.tip: Build strong basics and the Closed Hip Twist first; this version needs extra turn and tone to work.

variants.title: Advanced Hip Twist
variants.reason: The site gives no man's chart for this figure.

figures.name: Hip Twist Spiral
figures.summary: A hip twist that flows into a spiral for the lady, combining two Silver-level actions in one figure.
figures.tip: Practise the Open Hip Twist and the Spiral separately before you link them.

variants.title: Hip Twist Spiral
variants.reason: The site gives no man's chart for this figure.

figures.name: Turkish Towel
figures.summary: A playful figure in which both partners pass their hands over each other's head and shoulders as if drying with a towel.
figures.tip: Keep your frame soft and your arms low as you travel; it works best danced at the end of a bar.

variants.title: Turkish Towel
variants.reason: The site gives no man's chart for this figure.

figures.name: Sweetheart
figures.summary: A romantic figure in which partners trace a heart shape with their joined hands while moving in a close position.
figures.tip: Keep the hands soft and move together in time; use it for a short, showy moment in a routine.

variants.title: Sweetheart
variants.reason: The site gives no man's chart for this figure.

figures.name: Follow My Leader
figures.summary: A tandem pattern in which the lady follows the man across the floor in a straight line.
figures.tip: Keep both lines clear and look over your shoulder so the follower can see you; it is a floor-covering showpiece.

variants.title: Follow My Leader
variants.reason: The site gives no man's chart for this figure.

figures.name: Foot Changes
figures.summary: A footwork detail in which the weight changes between the feet in small shuffles, adding crisp rhythm to a basic or break.
figures.tip: Practise the shuffle on its own; keep the knees straight and weight forward over the balls of the feet.

variants.title: Foot Changes
variants.reason: The site gives no man's chart for this figure.

rumba.name: Rumba
rumba.music: Slow, romantic Latin ballads with a steady four-beat pulse and a languid feel.
rumba.movement_tip: Stay low and grounded with soft knees and let the hips move as each foot takes weight, with no rise and fall. Reach each step with a long, straight leg and a brushing foot.
rumba.position_tip: Closed hold is lighter and more relaxed than in Standard dances, with a little space between the partners and softer arms. Many figures use open or fan positions on one or two joined hands.

figures.name: Basic Movements
figures.summary: The basic movement is the core of rumba: forward and back on the same quick-quick-slow pattern. The closed, open and alternative versions all share one rhythm.
figures.tip: Hold the side step for its full two beats and use hip action rather than lift. It leads to New York, Spot Turns, Underarm Turns, Shoulder to Shoulder, Hand to Hand and the Fan.

variants.title: Open Basic Movement
variants.reason: the site's lady chart steps on the left foot twice in a row (steps 2 and 3), which no dancer can do; the game cannot reproduce the chart as printed

figures.name: Cucarachas
figures.summary: Cucarachas are small side presses with a quick recovery, danced in closed position. They give the dance a playful, grounded step.
figures.tip: Keep the pressed foot light so you can recover fast; you can repeat Cucarachas, move into Underarm Turns or finish with a basic.

figures.name: New York
figures.summary: The New York is a check-forward figure danced side by side, turning from one side-by-side position to the other. It is one of the first figures where you leave closed hold.
figures.tip: Make the check short and recover at once; afterwards you can repeat it, move to Spot Turns, Underarm Turns or Hand to Hand, or begin a Closed Hip Twist.

figures.name: Spot Turns
figures.summary: Spot Turns have each partner spin on the spot, he to the right and then left, while she does the opposite. They fit between basics and New Yorks.
figures.tip: Spin on the ball of the supporting foot and stay level; dance them after a basic or New York and follow with a basic.

figures.name: Underarm Turns to R & L
figures.summary: The underarm turn lets her spin left and then right beneath the raised joined hand while he dances a basic. It is the first step toward more turning figures.
figures.tip: Raise the hand early and keep it still; try it after Cucarachas, a basic or a New York.

figures.name: Shoulder to Shoulder
figures.summary: Shoulder to Shoulder angles the couple past one another's shoulder on each forward check, then returns to face each other. It is a compact figure from closed hold.
figures.tip: Keep the hold close so your shoulders almost touch as you pass; it follows a basic and leads on to another basic.

figures.name: Hand to Hand
figures.summary: Hand to Hand has both partners turn out to side-by-side and back to face each other, holding hands, first on one side and then the other.
figures.tip: Keep one hand joined throughout and stay level with her; it fits after a basic or New York and finishes with a basic.

figures.name: Progressive Walks
figures.summary: Progressive Walks travel six steps forward or backward, or side by side, in a quick-quick-slow pattern. They add travel to the otherwise spot-based dance.
figures.tip: Stretch each walk and hold the third and sixth steps; they pair with a basic before and after.

variants.title: Progressive Walks in Left Side Position
Progressive Walks in Right Side Position

figures.name: Side Steps
figures.summary: Side Steps are close-and-step moves along the floor to the left or right in closed hold. They are an easy, grounded way to travel.
figures.tip: Keep the steps small and the shoulders level; Side Steps to the left can follow Cucarachas and lead back into them.

figures.name: Cuban Rocks
figures.summary: Cuban Rocks are a rocking weight-change step with a side step then two in-place transfers. They give a relaxed rhythmic break from the walks.
figures.tip: Make the rock subtle and finish with a held weight transfer; they fit after New York or a basic.

figures.name: Fan
figures.summary: The Fan sends the lady away along his left into fan position, ending the closed basic with an opening movement. It is the entry to the Hockey Stick and Alemana.
figures.tip: Release the right hand early, extend your left arm slowly, and follow the Fan with a Hockey Stick or Alemana (you may also reach it after Cucarachas or a New York).

figures.name: Alemana
figures.summary: The Alemana starts in fan, walks the lady toward the man, then turns her right under the arm back to closed. It is a classic rumba turning figure.
figures.tip: Lead her past your left side before raising the hand; it follows a Fan and returns to a closed basic.

figures.name: Hockey Stick
figures.summary: The Hockey Stick is also danced from fan: she walks in, then turns left under his arm and steps back into open position. Its shape resembles a hockey stick.
figures.tip: Lower the hand as soon as she completes the turn; it follows a Fan and flows into basic movements.

figures.name: Natural Top
figures.summary: The Natural Top is a series of crossing-behind and side steps that rotate the couple right on the spot. It needs balance and small steps.
figures.tip: Keep the weight forward on the supporting foot and the steps small; the chart allows one to three turns, so start with one.

figures.name: Opening Out to R & L
figures.summary: Opening Out to R & L opens the lady first to his right and then to his left on each bar, from closed hold, bringing her back to closed each time.
figures.tip: Move the frame before the arm; follow it with a basic.

figures.name: Natural Opening Out
figures.summary: The Natural Opening Out sends her a half turn right, then back left, to face him. It is danced from closed hold with a small body turn.
figures.tip: Keep the body turn slight and let her travel; it fits after a basic or Closed Hip Twist preparation.

figures.name: Closed Hip Twist
figures.summary: The Closed Hip Twist turns her right then left across the front of the man and ends in fan. It leads naturally to a Hockey Stick or Alemana.
figures.tip: Lead her in front of your body, with firm left arm; after it dance a Hockey Stick or Alemana, and before it a New York.

figures.name: Open Hip Twist
figures.summary: The Open Hip Twist is danced from open facing position, ending in fan after she passes in front of the man and turns left. It is a Silver version of the hip twist.
figures.tip: Keep the small step on 4 small and the left arm quiet; dance a Hockey Stick or Alemana after it.

figures.name: Reverse Top
figures.summary: The Reverse Top spins the couple left on the spot with crossing and side steps, mirroring the Natural Top.
figures.tip: Keep the steps small and turn left evenly; pair it with a Natural Top or basic.

variants.title: Reverse Top
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Opening Out from Reverse Top
figures.summary: Opening Out from Reverse Top follows a Reverse Top: the couple opens out as she steps away, then comes back to closed.
figures.tip: Finish the reverse turn on balance before opening; dance it straight after a Reverse Top.

variants.title: Opening Out from Reverse Top
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Aida
figures.summary: The Aida is a Silver rumba figure where she passes by the man while he steps back and she walks around him, then returns to face him.
figures.tip: Keep your frame steady while she walks around; follow it with a basic.

variants.title: Aida
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Spiral
figures.summary: The Spiral is a Silver figure in which the lady winds up in a spiral turn while the man keeps stepping on the spot.
figures.tip: Keep the lead soft so she can rotate on the spot; end on a closed basic.

variants.title: Spiral
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Curl
figures.summary: The Curl is a Silver figure in which the man walks around the lady on a curved path while she turns beneath his arm.
figures.tip: Keep the arm shape clear and travel along a curve; dance it after a Fan or Alemana.

variants.title: Curl
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Rope Spinning
figures.summary: Rope Spinning is a Silver show figure where she spins repeatedly while the man leads the spinning with a rhythmic hand motion.
figures.tip: Spin around the same axis with a soft hand; build it after a basic or a Hip Twist.

variants.title: Rope Spinning

figures.name: Sliding Doors
figures.summary: Sliding Doors is a Gold figure in which the partners pass each other and part like doors before closing again.
figures.tip: Keep a clear frame as you separate and re-connect; dance it after a basic.

variants.title: Sliding Doors

figures.name: Fencing
figures.summary: Fencing is a Gold figure in which partners move toward and away from each other with lunging, side-by-side movements.
figures.tip: Keep the frame light and your weight over your lunging leg; follow it with a basic.

variants.title: Fencing

figures.name: Three Threes
figures.summary: Three Threes is a Gold figure of three groups of three steps that travel across the floor.
figures.tip: Count the groups carefully and keep each three steps even; use it after a basic.

figures.name: Three Alemanas
figures.summary: Three Alemanas chain three Alemana turns in a row, with the lady turning right three times.

figures.name: Advanced Hip Twist
figures.summary: Advanced Hip Twist is a Gold development of the hip twist, with a bigger turn for the lady.
figures.tip: Practise the Closed Hip Twist first; then lead the bigger turn with the body.

figures.name: Continuous Hip Twists
figures.summary: Continuous Hip Twists repeat the hip twist in a chain, with the lady turning repeatedly.
figures.tip: Keep the rhythm steady between twists; dance it after a Fan.

figures.name: Circular Hip Twists
figures.summary: Circular Hip Twists are Gold hip twists danced on a circular path around the man.
figures.tip: Walk a clear circle and keep the hand steady; dance it after a basic.

variants.title: Circular Hip Twists

jive.name: Jive
jive.music: Very fast, bouncy swing, rock and roll and boogie music.
jive.movement_tip: Stay on the balls of the feet with soft, bouncing knees and keep the steps small and sharp. The energy comes from the knee action, not from big steps.
jive.position_tip: Mostly closed hold or open facing with hands joined, light and elastic. The arms act as springs between you instead of pulling or pushing.

figures.name: Jive Basic In Place
figures.summary: The simplest jive pattern: a small rock in place followed by a chasse to each side. It teaches the bounce and timing everything else is built on.
figures.tip: Keep your weight forward over the balls of the feet and let the knees do the bounce. Follow it with a Fallaway Rock or use it to settle into the rhythm before an open figure.

variants.title: Jive Basic In Place
variants.reason: the site's lady chart repeats the right foot on steps 1 and 2 and then starts the chasse on it again (three right feet in a row, an evident typo), so her part cannot be danced as charted; the man's part alone is the usual mirror pattern

figures.name: Fallaway Rock
figures.summary: The classic fallaway opening: both rock back in a V shape, then close up again for a pair of chasses. It is the usual way to start from closed hold.
figures.tip: Rock back from the hips with a lifted chest, not by leaning. It leads naturally into a Throwaway, Change of Places, Whip or Walks, and can follow a Link.

figures.name: Fallaway Throwaway
figures.summary: A fallaway rock that travels into two chasses and sends her away to open facing hold. It is the standard way to break from closed hold.
figures.tip: Turn your body to the left to lead her out rather than pushing with the arm. Finish in open hold ready for a Link, Change of Places or Hands Behind Back.

figures.name: Link
figures.summary: A rock apart and a forward chasse that brings the couple from open facing hold back to closed hold. It is the connector between open figures and closed ones.
figures.tip: Draw her in on the first chasse with a soft elbow, not a pull. After it you can dance a Fallaway Rock, Throwaway, Whip or Walks.

figures.name: Change of Places R to L
figures.summary: A fallaway rock followed by a left-hand lift that turns her right to the other side of you. It moves the lady across to your left while you stay on the spot.
figures.tip: Raise the hand before the second chasse so she has time to turn. Afterwards you are in open hold, so link, change places the other way or dance a Hands Behind Back.

variants.title: Change of Places R to L

figures.name: Change of Places L to R
figures.summary: From open facing hold she crosses to your right side under the lifted left hand while you turn a little to the right. It is the partner to Change of Places Right to Left.
figures.tip: Hold your frame still and lift just enough for her to pass. Dance it after a Throwaway or Right to Left, and follow with a Link, American Spin or Hip Bump.

variants.title: Change of Places L to R

figures.name: Change of Hands Behind Back
figures.summary: From open hold you chasse past her and pass her right hand from one of your hands to the other behind your back. A showy but simple change of hands.
figures.tip: Make the turn small and keep the hands low while passing behind. You can reach it after a Throwaway or Change of Places, and follow it with a Link.

figures.name: Hip Bump
figures.summary: A playful figure where you turn to stand side by side, bump hips on the little beat, and turn back to face each other.
figures.tip: Keep your upper body still and only flick the hip on the quarter beat. It starts from open hold, so dance it after a Throwaway or Change of Places and follow it with a Link.

figures.name: American Spin
figures.summary: From open hold with the right hands joined, she spins a full turn to the right in front of you while you chasse in place. The most recognisable jive spin.
figures.tip: Give a small, clear push and then let go so she controls her own turn. Practise ending with the hands ready to retake hold; follow with a Link.

figures.name: Walks
figures.summary: Walks in promenade after the fallaway rock, either one step per beat or a chasse for each step. They travel forward and add a change of rhythm.
figures.tip: Think of long stalking steps on single counts and bouncy chasses on triples. They start like a Fallaway Rock from closed hold and end in promenade, so close the hold again with a Fallaway Rock.

figures.name: Stop and Go
figures.summary: A chasse as she turns left, then a pause and rock apart before she turns right on the way out. The stop gives the figure its name.
figures.tip: Make the pause crisp, then relax into the chasse. Start from open hold, for example after a Throwaway or Change of Places, and you end in open facing hold.

figures.name: Mooch
figures.summary: A long figure in side-by-side arm-to-arm positions with flicks and closes, danced once on the left and once on the right. A comic, rhythmic showpiece.
figures.tip: Keep the flicks low and quick and keep your arm snug against hers. It is entered from closed hold and ends there, so follow it with a Fallaway Rock.

figures.name: Whip
figures.summary: A fallaway rock, a turning chasse, then a Cuban cross and side step that whips her round before a final chasse. It can also be started from open hold.
figures.tip: Tuck the Cuban cross close to the standing foot so she can step between your feet. Follow it with a Throwaway or any closed-hold figure.

figures.name: Whip Throwaway
figures.summary: The Whip finished with a chasse in place, releasing her into open facing hold. It comes in versions starting from closed or open hold.
figures.tip: Do not let the whip lose its shape before the throw. Let the left arm extend slowly after the cross and follow it with a Link.

figures.name: Reverse Whip
figures.summary: A silver figure that uses the Whip pattern in the opposite direction. It is the mirror of the Whip.
figures.tip: Learn the Whip first and keep the same compact cross. Plan to use it after a closed-hold figure and follow it with a Link.

variants.title: Reverse Whip
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Windmill
figures.summary: A silver figure in which the lady turns around the man in a circle while he travels on a smaller arc, like a windmill.
figures.tip: Keep your arm frame steady and let her do the walking. Use it after a Link and finish by drawing her back to closed hold.

variants.title: Windmill
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Spanish Arms
figures.summary: A silver figure in which she passes under his arm with her arms crossed, so both sets of arms wrap in front of her.
figures.tip: Keep the arms low and avoid tightening the hold. Start from open hold and unwind with a Link.

variants.title: Spanish Arms
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Rolling Off The Arm
figures.summary: A silver figure where she rolls across his arms from one side to the other, linked together as she turns.
figures.tip: Keep a firm frame so the arms act as a track for her. Dance it from an open figure and end with a Link.

variants.title: Rolling Off The Arm

figures.name: Simple Spin
figures.summary: A silver figure in which she makes a simple turn in front of him on the spot, a small step up from the American Spin.
figures.tip: Keep the turn on the spot and finish facing her. Combine it after an American Spin or a Change of Places.

samba.name: Samba
samba.music: Brazilian carnival music at a steady medium pace, with a firm accent on every first beat.
samba.movement_tip: Bend and straighten the knees in a continuous springing action, so each bar bounces on the 1 and lifts through the a. The hips stay relaxed and the upper body calm.
samba.position_tip: Closed hold is slightly looser than in Standard, with the lady a little to his right. Promenade, open and side-by-side shapes are used for walks, voltas and rocks.

figures.name: Natural Basic Movement
figures.summary: The first samba step: a forward and a back basic in closed hold, with the characteristic bounce. It is the anchor most other figures start from and return to.
figures.tip: Learn the bounce before the steps, then use this figure as your home base. It flows into Whisks, Side Basic, Reverse Basic, Traveling Bota Fogos, Closed Rocks and Corta Jaca.

figures.name: Side Samba Walk

figures.summary: A bota fogo pattern in promenade with joined hands, where the partners swap sides, the lady crossing in front of the man. It is a flashy way to pass each other.
figures.tip: Raise the joined hands before the pass and keep them high, so the lady travels cleanly in front. It follows a Side Samba Walk and leads back to Samba Walks in PP.

figures.name: Shadow Botafogos
figures.summary: Botafogos danced in shadow position with both partners walking forward in the same direction. A showy, playful pattern.
figures.tip: Keep your two bodies in one line. Match her steps and timing exactly, as no hold links you.

figures.name: Shadow Traveling Voltas

figures.tip: Stay close behind her and start every cross together; if the couple drifts out of line the picture is lost.

figures.name: Shadow Samba Walks
figures.summary: Samba walks danced in shadow position, with both partners walking the same feet in the same direction.
figures.tip: Match her foot, her timing and her knee action, step for step. It links well with the other shadow figures.

figures.name: Reverse Turn
figures.summary: A closed-hold turn to the left covering nearly a full turn, built from a forward side-cross bar and a back-close-replace bar. It is the main left-turning figure of the syllabus.
figures.tip: Turn the body late: the feet do most of the work in the first bar and the body completes the turn on the last step. It follows a Reverse Basic and can lead into Bota Fogos or Closed Rocks.

figures.name: Corta Jaca
figures.summary: A rocking figure in closed hold: one strong step forward, then three rocking steps with a slide to replace the weight each time. It adds a sharp, rhythmic accent to the routine.
figures.tip: Make the first step the strongest and slide the foot across for every replace. You can arrive at it from a Natural Basic, Side Basic or Whisks, and leave into a Side Basic or Whisks.

preceded_by.name: Traveling Bota Fogo Forward on LF

figures.name: Closed Rocks
figures.summary: Two rocking steps forward in closed hold, the man rocking forward and the lady back, on the counts 1, 2 and &. A compact, rhythmic figure.
figures.tip: Rock from the knees and keep the steps small. It combines easily with the Natural Basic, Reverse Basic, Reverse Turn and Corta Jaca, or itself.

figures.name: Open Rocks
figures.summary: A pair of rocking steps forward in an open shape, the man sending the lady out and back with turns to the right and then to the left. It plays with distance between the partners.
figures.tip: Give her a clear lead for each turn and take the hold back on the next count 1. It sits well after a Closed Rocks or Reverse Turn, or before a Basic.

figures.name: Back Rocks
figures.summary: Rocking steps danced backward by the man in closed hold, turning slightly left and then right. It travels the couple back along the diagonal.
figures.tip: Keep your chest lifted and your rocks small. Use it to change direction between a forward figure and a back figure.

figures.name: Plait
figures.summary: Ten small back steps for the man in a single line while the lady swivels forward, brushing the feet. It is a playful figure in which the partners stay almost in one place.
figures.tip: Rehearse the swivel-and-brush action alone first. It needs a firm frame so that the man's tiny steps do not fall out of time.

variants.title: Plait
variants.reason: the lady's chart lists a foot sequence that repeats a foot in the second half, and each of her steps is a swivel with a brush; the game's weight rules cannot dance it as charted

figures.name: Rolling Off The Arm
figures.summary: A figure begun in sweetheart (shadow-like) position where the man leads the lady in a whisk and she rolls off his arm to the side and back. It uses side-by-side positions.
figures.tip: Wrap the arm around her waist again as the second whisk finishes, so the hold is restored cleanly.

variants.title: Rolling Off The Arm
variants.reason: it starts in sweetheart position, with partners side by side and the lady on his right, which has no hold in the game

figures.name: Argentine Crosses
figures.summary: A long turning figure to the right in closed hold, in which both partners step forward on cruzado-style crossing steps. It makes almost a full circle.
figures.tip: Keep the hold close and let both bodies follow the circle. Lead it from a Basic or Closed Rocks and finish with a Basic.

figures.name: Maypole
figures.summary: A figure in which the man circles around the lady with voltas while she turns on the spot under raised joined hands, like dancing round a maypole. It is danced in either direction.
figures.tip: Keep your joined hands high and still, as she is the pole. After it you return to closed hold for a Basic or Whisk, or into open position.

figures.name: Shadow Circular Voltas
figures.summary: Circular voltas danced as a pair in shadow position, the man turning left in the first half and right in the second, with the lady staying on his right.
figures.tip: Stay in step with her and keep your shoulders in line, so the two bodies look like one.

variants.title: Shadow Circular Voltas
variants.reason: shadow position (partners side by side, facing the same way) has no hold in the game

figures.name: Contra Bota Fogos
figures.summary: A Gold-level bota fogo pattern in which the partners move against each other, in contrary directions, instead of side by side.
figures.tip: Master the Traveling and Criss Cross Bota Fogos first; the contra version asks for the same quick side-and-replace footwork with more precise timing between you.

variants.title: Contra Bota Fogos
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart or lady's chart for this figure

figures.name: Roundabout
figures.summary: A Gold-level travelling figure in which the couple circles as they progress, sometimes called a roundabout.
figures.tip: Keep the bounce going through every step and keep the circle small, so the pair stays together in its turning.

variants.title: Roundabout
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart or lady's chart for this figure

figures.name: Natural Roll
figures.summary: A Gold-level turning figure to the right with the lady's body and hips rolling through the steps. It is danced in closed hold.
figures.tip: Work on a smooth, continuous rolling feel from the ribs and hips, not from the arms, and practise the Natural Basic until the bounce is automatic.

variants.title: Natural Roll

figures.name: Reverse Roll
figures.summary: The mirror of the Natural Roll: a Gold-level turning figure to the left, with the same rolling hips.
figures.tip: Learn the Natural Roll first, then reverse the turn; keep the hold steady and the knees soft.

figures.name: Promenade and Counter Promenade Runs
figures.summary: Gold-level quick running steps in promenade and counter promenade, in which the couple travels along the line of dance.
figures.tip: Keep the steps small and the feet low so the runs stay light and tidy. Build up to it with Samba Walks and Bota Fogos to promenade.

figures.name: Three Step Turn
figures.summary: A Gold-level turn that is built from just three steps, danced as a quick turning action.
figures.tip: Place each step precisely and keep the body steady, as the turn comes from the hips and feet together.

figures.name: Samba Locks
figures.summary: A Gold-level figure of locking steps, in which one foot crosses the other in a quick lock while the couple travels.
figures.tip: Keep each lock tight and quick and the bounce continuous. Walks in promenade and Bota Fogos are good practice before this.

figures.name: Cruzados Walks and Locks
figures.summary: A Gold-level figure combining crossing walks with locking steps. It travels along the line of dance.
figures.tip: Cross cleanly and keep the knees soft, so the steps do not become heavy. Learn the Samba Locks first.

paso.name: Paso Doble
paso.music: Bold, dramatic bullfight marches in 2/4, with Espana Cani as the classic tune.
paso.movement_tip: Keep the chest high and the shoulders level, with small, firm steps on the balls of the feet and no rise and fall. The man is the matador and the woman his cape.
paso.position_tip: Closed hold is tight and upright, with the man's frame strong and the woman tucked slightly to his right. Promenade and counter promenade shapes are shown with the head and chest, not by loosening the arms.

figures.name: Appel
figures.summary: The appel is a short stamp of the foot that opens many Paso figures and marks the downbeat like a matador's challenge. It is a basic building block rather than a figure of its own.
figures.tip: Press the whole foot down quietly, keep the knee soft and use it as the first step of figures such as the Chasses, Promenade and Separation.

variants.title: Appel
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Sur Place
figures.summary: Marching on the spot, one step per beat, in closed or semi-closed hold. It is the neutral figure of the dance and the easiest way to fill time between steps.
figures.tip: Press the balls of the feet down on every count and keep your head still. It can come before and after almost every figure, so use it to wait for the music.

figures.name: Drag
figures.summary: A single low, wide step to the side with a slow, controlled draw of the feet over three beats. It gives the dance a dramatic pause with a promenade-style shape.
figures.tip: Bend the knees on the step and stand up only as the feet meet on count 4. It goes well before Basic Movements, Chasses or Separations.

figures.name: Deplacement / Attack
figures.summary: A forward march that starts either with a step (the deplacement) or an appel (the attack). It is danced without turn or with up to a quarter turn left, and a slip version starts with a turning slip.
figures.tip: Decide at the start whether you attack with a stamp or a step, and keep counts 2 to 4 identical. It chains with the Chasses, Sur Place and Promenade, and the quarter turn ends facing the centre.

figures.name: Promenade Link
figures.summary: A short link of appel, side and across in promenade, closing with a turn to face the centre. It brings a couple from line of dance into the promenade shape and out again.
figures.tip: Finish the turn with your upper body on count 4 so the hold is square again. It combines with Sur Place, Basic Movement and Chasses and can follow the second half of an Ecart.

figures.name: Promenade
figures.summary: The first big Paso shape: out into promenade, a turn into closed hold, then a travelling walk and quarter turn. It is the classic figure for showing the matador and cape.
figures.tip: Show the promenade line with the head and chest on counts 2 and 3. It follows most marches and Separations, and can be followed by Ecart, Sixteen or Separation.

figures.name: Ecart
figures.summary: A forward walk that ends in a fallaway shape moving against the line of dance. It sets up the pair for a Huit or Grand Circle.
figures.tip: Do not stretch the last back step; keep it small so you can start the next figure at once. The site follows it only with Huit, Grand Circle or Promenade Link.

figures.name: Separation
figures.summary: The man marches in place while the woman is sent away and brought back. It is the first figure that really opens the hold and highlights the lady as the cape.
figures.tip: Lower the joined hands slowly to send her and retract them evenly as she returns. Danced from many figures, it leads on to the Caping Walks version, the Fallaway Ending or a Promenade.

preceded_by.name: Chasses to Left
preceded_by.condition: Close RF to LF (Lady's LF to RF) into a LF Sur Place, then continue into Separation.

figures.name: Separation with Lady's Caping Walks
figures.summary: A longer Separation in which the man raises the joined hands and the lady walks round behind his back before they close. It shows off the cape idea.
figures.tip: Raise the arm only when she reaches your right side and keep marching evenly. It starts from Separation and can lead into Basic Movements, Chasses, Sixteen or Promenade.

preceded_by.name: Chasses to Left
preceded_by.condition: Close RF to LF (Lady's LF to RF) into a LF Sur Place, then continue into Separation with Lady's Caping Walks.

figures.name: Separation with Fallaway Ending
figures.summary: A Separation followed by a fallaway ending where both pass forward, turn right and step back in the fallaway shape. It adds a dramatic final shape to the opening.
figures.tip: Take her into your right arm as the walks begin and keep the fallaway tall. It follows a Separation and then may lead into most closed-hold figures.

followed_by.name: Chasses to Left
followed_by.condition: Close RF to LF (Lady LF to RF) into a LF Sur Place, then continue into Separation with Fallaway Ending.

figures.name: Huit
figures.summary: The woman circles a figure of eight round the man while he marches on the spot. It starts in promenade position and ends in normal hold.
figures.tip: March on the spot and stay still above the waist so she can see your line. It follows Promenade-type figures that end to the side in promenade, and leads into almost anything else.

followed_by.name: Chasses to Left
followed_by.condition: Close RF to LF (Lady LF to RF) into a LF Sur Place, then continue into Huit.

figures.name: Sixteen
figures.summary: A promenade pattern followed by a long march on the spot while the woman weaves round the man twice. It takes a full sixteen beats.
figures.tip: Keep your frame strong through the long march so the shaping holds. It joins to the basic marches and Chasses and can be followed by Promenade, Ecart or Sixteen again.

figures.name: Promenade and Counter Promenade

figures.tip: Make the change of shape clear at count 5 with the head and chest. It leads into Promenade, Huit or Grand Circle, which all begin in promenade.

figures.name: Grand Circle
figures.summary: A promenade-position figure where the man twists half a turn in place while the lady circles him. It finishes in closed hold facing the line of dance.
figures.tip: Hold the cross for three beats, then let the feet uncross smoothly in the twist. It follows an Ecart, a Promenade and Counter Promenade or an Open Telemark and can be followed by most basic figures.

figures.name: Open Telemark

figures.tip: Keep the turn for the side step and the swivel and stay low through the middle. Danced from closed hold, it may lead into Sur Place, Promenade or Separation.

am_chacha.name: American Style Cha Cha
am_chacha.music: Bright, medium-tempo Latin music with a steady beat; the cha cha lands its quick triple step on the last beat of every bar.
am_chacha.movement_tip: Keep the knees soft and let the hips settle into each step, with small, quick chasses and crisp rocks on 2 and 3.
am_chacha.position_tip: Dance in closed or open facing hold, with one- or two-hand connections that stay springy so the lead travels through the arms.

figures.name: Cha Cha Basic Movement
figures.summary: The foundation of American cha cha: two rock steps, each followed by a side chasse, danced facing your partner either in closed hold or at arm's length.
figures.tip: Keep the rocks small and the chasses compact; the figure flows into almost anything, so practise it before and after Progressive Basic, Open Break, Underarm Turns and Crossover Breaks.

figures.name: Inverted Crossovers
figures.summary: A crossover variation in which the man rocks back on the left while the lady rocks forward, with a quarter turn each way around the chasses.
figures.tip: Keep a two-hand connection through the quarter turns; it follows crossover breaks or a basic and finishes ready for any open figure.

figures.name: Stop and Go
figures.summary: The man rocks back away from the lady, replaces and chasses left, then rocks forward on the right while she goes back, finishing in open facing position.
figures.tip: Keep a light left hand on the first rock so she stops and returns on count 3; it comes after a basic or underarm turn and leaves you in open facing position.

figures.name: Underarm Pass
figures.summary: A hand-passing figure: after a rock and a forward chasse for her, the man passes his raised hand over her head as they change places, finishing in open facing position.
figures.tip: Raise the left hand a beat before you pass it over her head; follow it with Crossover Breaks or a basic once you are in open position.

figures.name: Back Spot Turn
figures.summary: A continuous turn on the spot in closed hold, alternating a crossed-behind step with a side step through the whole bar pattern.
figures.tip: Keep the steps tiny and your frame still, letting the turn come from the body; dance it from a closed basic and finish with a basic.

figures.name: The Chase
figures.summary: A playful figure danced apart with no hold: partners walk and chasse towards each other, then dance a progressive basic apart.
figures.tip: Get Progressive Basic secure first, since the Chase repeats it apart from your partner; keep the same step length so you stay in time together.

variants.title: Chase Half Turns

variants.title: Chase Full Turn

figures.name: Open Left Turn
figures.summary: A Beginning Silver turn in open position, going by its name a left turn; the site's chart page returned an error, so no steps are converted.

figures.name: Crossover Side Breaks
figures.summary: A long crossover combination in which each side has a forward rock beside the partner followed by a side rock facing, danced to the left and then to the right.
figures.tip: Change hands during the chasses so the next side is ready; it follows crossover breaks or a basic and goes back to a basic or a cross-body lead.

figures.name: 5th Position Side Break
figures.summary: A fifth-position break danced twice in a row with a small side rock in between, so the couple opens into fallaway and closes again.
figures.tip: Use only an eighth of a turn each way and keep the hold; it follows a basic or Fifth Position Breaks and leaves you ready for any closed figure.

figures.name: Cross-Body Lead w/ Underarm Turn L.

figures.tip: Make the Cross-Body Lead clean first, then lift the hand on the final chasse; finish in open position for crossover breaks or a basic.

figures.name: Checked Underarm Turn to Right

figures.tip: Time the check so she steps forward on 2 and replaces on 3; it begins like the Open Break and finishes in open facing position.

figures.name: Cha Cha Variation 1
figures.summary: A long gold routine of about thirty-seven steps that goes into sweetheart position, includes a checked step with a ronde, and ends with the lady turning right over three steps.

figures.name: Cha Cha Variation 2

am_rumba.name: American Style Rumba
am_rumba.music: Medium-tempo Latin music with a slow, sensual pulse and a clear beat to settle each step on.
am_rumba.movement_tip: Keep a soft Cuban motion: the hips settle sideways as each step takes weight, and the knee bends and straightens smoothly. Travel on the ball of the foot and let the heel lower as you take the weight.
am_rumba.position_tip: Closed hold is relaxed and close, and open facing with one or two hands is just as common. Promenade and side-by-side shapes appear in walks, crossovers and spot turns.

figures.name: Rumba Box
figures.summary: The core six-step pattern of the Rumba, a walk and a side close forward and then back. It is the home base for most Bronze work.
figures.tip: Settle the weight on each step with a hip action before moving on. Repeat the Box as often as you like, then leave it into 8-Count Underarm Turn, Cross-Body Lead or Cuban Walks.

figures.name: Alternative Basic
figures.summary: A basic that opens each half with a side step and then rocks, so it can replace the Box or be used for variety. It opens many of the Bronze breaks.
figures.tip: Keep the rocks small and the weight over the standing foot. It leads naturally to Side Breaks, Open Break & Underarm Turn, the Crossover figures and Fifth Position Breaks.

figures.name: Side Breaks
figures.summary: A pair of side rocks, one to each side, ending with a close. It is the Cucaracha idea in Rumba timing.
figures.tip: Press out lightly to the side and push back quickly, then close in time. Use it after an Alternative Basic when you want a stationary moment.

figures.name: Cuban Walks
figures.summary: Three-step walks in slow, quick, quick time, forward or back in closed hold, or forward in promenade or counter promenade. They give the dance travel.
figures.tip: Roll through the foot and let the hips swing with each walk. Take them after a Rumba Box or Alternative Basic and leave them into another Box.

figures.name: Open Break & Underarm Turn
figures.summary: A short break apart for both partners, then her turn to the right beneath his lifted hand. Couples nearly always dance the two halves as one figure.
figures.tip: Raise the hand during the second half and keep it still. It follows an Alternative Basic and can lead into more basics.

figures.name: 8-Count Underarm Turn
figures.summary: The popular eight-count turn: half a box, then a slow walk-around for the lady under his arm, and a finishing half box. It is a staple for social dancers.
figures.tip: Make the walk-around slow and wide so she never rushes. Start it from a Rumba Box and finish into another Box.

figures.name: Crossover Breaks Forward
figures.summary: A pair of crossover breaks danced side by side and ending face to face. It is borrowed from the Cha Cha.
figures.tip: Turn together on the first step and check forward lightly. Start from an Alternative Basic and keep your hands joined all the way through.

figures.name: Crossover Back Breaks
figures.summary: A crossover break danced with the rock going backward instead of forward, in side-by-side shape. It offers an easy variety after an Alternative Basic.
figures.tip: Turn together on the step before the rock and keep the back rock small. Use it after an Alternative Basic and repeat it or go back into the basic.

figures.name: Crossover Turns
figures.summary: A crossover that grows into full circles: both partners walk a complete turn in opposite directions and meet again facing each other.
figures.tip: Keep the walking steps even and make each circle a single smooth curve. It starts from an Alternative Basic and repeats left then right.

figures.name: Fifth Position Breaks
figures.summary: A rock step in fifth position (one foot tucked behind the other) taken from the side, either repeated to both sides or finishing into a Box.
figures.tip: Keep the fifth-position step short and the toe turned out, then recover quickly. Both versions follow an Alternative Basic or Side Breaks.

figures.name: Cross-Body Lead
figures.summary: The classic American Rumba figure in which the leader turns away and the lady crosses in front of him. It starts like a Box and finishes in a left turn.
figures.tip: Open the way for her before you turn left, then keep the left hand steady as she passes. Begin it from a Rumba Box and continue with another Box or Walks.

figures.name: Alternative Cross-Body Lead
figures.summary: A cross-body lead that grows from the Alternative Basic rather than the Box, in a shorter eight-beat pattern.
figures.tip: Set the rock before the turn, and turn your body, not your arm, to send her across. It follows an Alternative Basic.

figures.name: Cuban Rocks
figures.summary: Tiny rocking steps forward or backward that stress hip action over travel. They are an alternative to Cuban Walks.
figures.tip: Keep each rock under the body and let the hips settle. Forward Rocks follow a Rumba Box; Backward Rocks follow an Alternative Basic.

figures.name: Offset Breaks
figures.summary: Rocking steps taken in offset, passing first on one side of the partner and then the other. Also known as Shoulder to Shoulder.
figures.tip: Angle each forward rock past her shoulder and turn the shoulders only a little. It comes after an Alternative Basic.

figures.name: Back Spot Turn
figures.summary: The spot turn danced with the leader stepping side and cross behind while the lady walks forward round him. It comes in a full six-step form, two short endings and a version with her underarm turn.
figures.tip: Keep your own steps tiny and make the lady do the travelling around you. Start it from a Rumba Box or Alternative Basic and use an ending to leave it.

variants.title: Back Spot Turn w/ Underarm Turn to L

figures.name: Forward Spot Turn
figures.summary: The mirror image of the Back Spot Turn: the leader steps forward between her feet and turns left while she steps side and cross behind.
figures.tip: Step across between her feet with the toe turned out, and turn from the legs. Use it from a Box and leave it into another basic.

figures.name: Spot Turn in Two Directions
figures.summary: A spot turn that reverses direction part-way: half a Forward Spot Turn, an offset check, then half a Back Spot Turn.
figures.tip: Stop the first turn cleanly with the check before reversing. It combines the two basic spot turns.

figures.name: Cross Body Lead to Underarm Turn Left
figures.summary: A Cross-Body Lead followed by a further step that sends the lady into a left underarm turn.
figures.tip: Complete the cross body before you raise the left hand so her turn starts from the right place. Follow it with a Box or other basic.

figures.name: Circling Cuban Walks
figures.summary: A long pattern based on the Cross-Body Lead in which the pair walks in a wide curve side by side before the leader draws the lady back. Two shorter versions use her underarm turn to leave the walks.
figures.tip: Keep the circle even and the left-hand connection light. Enter from a Cross-Body Lead and leave into a Rumba Box.

figures.name: Cuban Wrap

figures.tip: Keep your right hand on her back and the left hand at her eye level through the walks. Enter after a basic and leave into another basic.

figures.name: Open Left Turn
figures.summary: A left-turning figure built from rocks taken outside the partner, first on one side and then the other. It has a regular version, one with the slow on the side step, and one with a swivel.
figures.tip: Keep each rock small and turn only on the side steps. Dance it after a Rumba Box or Alternative Basic and leave it into another basic.

figures.name: Crossover Side Breaks
figures.summary: A longer version of the crossover break with the rock danced to the side, once each way, ending face to face.
figures.tip: Recover fully on each replace so the side steps stay light. It follows an Alternative Basic and is used when you want two crossovers in one figure.

figures.name: Fifth Position Side Break
figures.summary: A rock step in fifth position taken to the side and repeated, in the style of a side break.
figures.tip: Keep the fifth position tight and the weight changes quick. Use it after an Alternative Basic or Box.

swing.name: East Coast Swing
swing.music: Bright, bouncy swing, jump blues and rock-and-roll tunes with a strong backbeat.
swing.movement_tip: Keep the knees soft and bounce with the beat, keeping the steps small and the triples light. The accent falls on 2 of the rock step, so settle into it.
swing.position_tip: Dance in closed hold or open facing hold with an elastic, springy frame; the arms stretch a little on each rock step and return, never pulling.

figures.name: Basic Step - Open Position
figures.summary: The simplest swing pattern: two chasses to the sides and a rock step apart, danced in open facing hold. It is the foundation every other six-count figure is built on.
figures.tip: Stay light on the balls of the feet and let the rock step stretch the arms. Dance it to find the bounce, then follow it with an Underarm Turn or a Link to Closed Position.

figures.name: Basic Step - Closed Hold
figures.summary: The same two chasses and rock step in closed hold, with the rock taken in fallaway so both partners step back in line. It is the standard closed-hold basic.
figures.tip: Open into fallaway just for the rock and close up again for the next chasse. It leads into a Throwout, a tuck-in turn or the Lindy figures.

figures.name: Throwout
figures.summary: The usual way to leave closed hold: a left-turning basic that sends her forward past your left side and releases her into open facing hold.
figures.tip: Turn your body to the left on the first chasse so the turn sends her out, not the arm. Dance it after a closed basic, then follow with an underarm turn or the open basic.

figures.name: Link to Closed Position
figures.summary: A basic that starts in open facing hold and draws her in to closed hold, finishing with a rock in fallaway. It is the standard way to close up.
figures.tip: Bring her in on the first chasse and take hold on the second. Dance it after any open figure and follow it with a closed basic or throwout.

figures.name: Underarm Turn to R.
figures.summary: The first underarm turn: she travels under the raised left hand and turns three quarters to the right while you turn a quarter left. A staple of the dance.
figures.tip: Lift the hand on the first chasse and keep it up until she faces you. Dance it after the open basic and follow it with the Underarm Turn to Left.

figures.name: Underarm Turn to L.
figures.summary: The partner to the turn to the right: she turns three quarters to the left under the raised hand while you turn a quarter right.
figures.tip: Start raising the hand as soon as the first chasse begins. It works after the turn to the right, a basic or a link, and leads on to another basic or a loop.

figures.name: Hammerlock
figures.summary: A two-part figure in which she turns right under your hand and her left arm wraps behind her back, then she unwinds the other way. The hands never let go.
figures.tip: Lower the low hand a little and rotate it before the arm wraps, and keep the rock step small. Start it from open facing hold with two hands joined.

figures.name: Cuddle Wrap
figures.summary: A two-part figure that wraps her into your arms beside you after a left turn, then unwraps her to the right. The hands stay joined throughout.
figures.tip: Keep the arms low and loose while she wraps in, and keep the chasse back short. Begin it from open facing hold with two hands joined.

figures.name: Back Pass
figures.summary: She passes behind your back while you both turn about a half, finishing in open facing hold with a change of hands. The charted version uses a single hand change.
figures.tip: Let her right hand rest on your waist and keep the arm free to take it. Dance it after a basic or an underarm turn; the hold finishes right to right.

variants.title: Back Pass with Single Hand Change
Back Pass with Double Hand Change
variants.reason: the site gives no steps for this variant (only the hold changes are described)

figures.name: Alternating Underarm Turns
figures.summary: Two underarm turns in a row: she turns left under your raised hand, then you turn left under your own raised hand while she turns right. Both partners turn a half each time.
figures.tip: Use the lowered hand to guide her past while you turn. It can be repeated or mixed with the open basic and the single underarm turns.

figures.name: Single Overhead Loop
figures.summary: An underarm turn to the left where the joined hands loop over your head and drop behind your neck, ending with a hand slide into a new hold.
figures.tip: Let the hands pass behind your head only after she has passed. It ends in a different hold from the one it started in, so follow it with an open basic.

figures.name: Double Overhead Loop
figures.summary: An open basic in which both of you turn a quarter left, loop the joined hands behind your heads, then turn back and slide hands to a right-to-right hold.
figures.tip: Lift the hands as you replace on the rock step before and lower them behind the heads on the first chasse. Follow it with the American spin or open basic.

variants.title: Double Overhead Loop
variants.reason: the site's lady chart repeats the man's rock-step feet (left back, right replace), so after her left-foot chasse she would have to step on the same foot twice

figures.name: Closed Tuck-In Turn Turn
figures.summary: A tuck-in turn from closed hold: you tuck her in toward you, then push gently and release so she spins on her own through a compact chasse.
figures.tip: Build the tension in the left arm on the first chasse and release only after count 2. Dance it after a closed basic and follow with a link or open basic.

figures.name: American Spin Tuck-In
figures.summary: The American Spin: from a right-to-right hold you tuck her in, then give a small push so she spins a full turn on the spot while you chasse in place.
figures.tip: Brace the right arm during the tuck, then let go after count 2 so she turns freely. It can be repeated with the right-to-right hold, or followed by an open basic.

figures.name: Shoulder Spin Tuck-In
figures.summary: A spin led from her shoulders: you turn behind her on the first chasse, then guide her into a travelling spin over three tiny steps.
figures.tip: Hold her upper arms lightly and release early. Follow it with an open basic or a link, and dance it after an open figure such as the basic.

figures.name: Continuous Tuck-In Turn
figures.summary: A chain of tuck-in turns in which she is led round to your front and back again, one turn after another.
figures.tip: Keep the right-to-right hold springy so each tuck is led clearly. Use the single tuck-in turns first, then link them together.

variants.title: Continuous Tuck-In Turn
variants.reason: the chart is a bare four-chasse outline in shadow position with no turns, holds or rock step, which the game's holds cannot show

figures.name: Lindy Basic Turning to Right
figures.summary: The Lindy-timed turning basic from promenade: you chasse diagonally and cross behind before turning right through a second chasse. Two variations add her underarm turn.
figures.tip: Count it in eight, with a rock cross and step in the middle; keep the cross small. It begins like a closed basic's rock step and ends in promenade ready for another figure.

variants.title: Lindy Right Turn w/ UAT to R.
Lindy Right Turn w/ UAT to L.

figures.name: Lindy Basic Turning to Left
figures.summary: The partner of the right-turning Lindy basic, turning left: you walk forward round her while she chasses diagonally and crosses behind.
figures.tip: Curve around her on the two walking steps. It starts in promenade and ends in promenade, so you can follow it with a throwout or another closed figure.

figures.name: Lindy Side Passes
figures.summary: A twenty-count figure of repeated side chasses with rock steps back and across, so you and she pass each other on alternating sides in open hold.
figures.tip: Make each rock back and across small and keep the same line. Use it after a basic or an underarm turn and finish with the open basic.

figures.name: Stop & Go
figures.summary: A Lindy-timed figure where you chasse forward, step across her path and replace to stop her in cross-body position, then chasse out again.
figures.tip: Make the stop crisp and the second chasse relaxed. Dance it from open facing hold and follow with a basic or another Lindy pattern.

figures.name: Fallaway Walks
figures.summary: A closed basic whose rock step becomes two walks back in fallaway; the longer version adds four walks back and then points and sidesteps.
figures.tip: Keep your frame while you walk back and think of the points as light taps. The simple version fits between closed figures, the long one is a showpiece.

variants.title: Fallaway Walks & Points
variants.reason: the site's lady chart starts her four backward walks on the left foot although her second chasse ends on it, so her part cannot be danced as charted

figures.name: Double Underarm Turn to R.

figures.tip: Learn the single Underarm Turn to Right first. Raise the hand early and keep it up for the whole double turn.

figures.name: Double Underarm Turn to L.

bolero.name: Bolero
bolero.music: Slow, romantic Latin ballads with a long, lingering pulse that invites rising and sinking through each step.
bolero.movement_tip: Bolero is built on rising and lowering: swell up gently over each slow, and sink into the knee as the quick rock settles. Keep the hips soft but let the body rise and fall do the talking.
bolero.position_tip: Most figures start in a relaxed closed hold or in open facing with joined hands. Contact figures stay body to body, while the open figures give the lady room to turn and travel.

figures.name: Basic Movement
figures.summary: The Bolero Basic: six steps with a rising slow and two quick rock steps, danced in closed hold, in contact, or ending open. It is the foundation of nearly all Bolero.
figures.tip: Think rise on the slow, sink on the quick-quick. Follow it with an underarm turn or the open ending, which leads straight into the progressive basic.

figures.name: Progressive Basic
figures.summary: An open facing version of the basic where the slows go back and forward rather than to the side, so the couple progresses along the line.
figures.tip: Keep the joined hands level and quiet. Use the ended-closed ending to come back into hold after the basic's open ending.

figures.name: Hip Lifts
figures.summary: A stylised basic in which the rock steps become a stationary hip lift, danced in contact hold.
figures.tip: Keep the weight over the supporting leg and let the lifted hip be the only movement; it follows the basic well.

figures.name: Underarm Turn to Right
figures.summary: The lady turns right under the man's raised left hand while he dances a back rock; it can be done on the spot or with the progressive basic.
figures.tip: Lift the hand on the slow count, before her quick. Lead it from the basic, then lower the hand and close up over steps 4-5.

figures.name: Crossover Breaks Forward
figures.summary: A crossover break danced in open position, passing through promenade and counter promenade with a forward rock on each side.
figures.tip: Release one hand at a time so the partners stay linked. Come into it from open facing and finish back in open facing.

figures.name: Crossover Back Breaks
figures.summary: The crossover break danced backward, with the rock steps taken back in side-by-side shapes. It sits beside the forward version in open facing.
figures.tip: Take the first quick back with a small step. Alternate it with the forward crossover so the pair keeps changing sides.

figures.name: Crossover Turns
figures.summary: A crossover break in which each partner makes a half turn on the third and sixth steps, finishing facing and ready for the next open figure.
figures.tip: Spot the half turn on the quick; keep the two quicks tight and the slow for the rise.

figures.name: Fifth Position Breaks
figures.summary: A break pattern where the rocks are taken in crossed fifth position, passing through fallaway and promenade shapes. It can start closed or open.
figures.tip: Close the feet fully in fifth and keep the steps small. Use it to travel into a closed-hold figure such as the basic.

figures.name: Underarm Pass
figures.summary: She passes forward under his raised left hand and turns left to face him, while he steps side and crosses behind.
figures.tip: Draw the left hand in before you lift it, so she gets a clear signal. Follow it with a basic or a side pass.

figures.name: Side Pass
figures.summary: She is led past his left side while he turns left, then she makes a half turn left to face him again.
figures.tip: Aim the arm slightly left and keep your rock small so the lady has a clean lane. It pairs well with the underarm pass.

figures.name: Man's Underarm Turn
figures.summary: The man turns right under his own raised hand while the lady walks back, then draws her past in a cross-body shape.
figures.tip: Raise the joined hands before you duck under. Follow it with a cross-body style figure or return to the basic.

figures.name: Sit Break to Underarm Turn to R.
figures.summary: A sit break, where the man sinks over one leg with the other extended, leading into an underarm turn to the lady's right.
figures.tip: Keep your weight on the standing leg through the sit, then switch smoothly on the slow. Pair with the basic before and after.

variants.title: Sit Break to Underarm Turn to R.
variants.reason: the chart keeps the man's weight on his right foot while the left foot extends or the position is held, and the game's step model cannot dance a step on the supporting foot

figures.name: Sit Break to Hip Twist Side Pass
figures.summary: The same sit break, followed by a hip twist that sends the lady past his left side into open facing.
figures.tip: Retract the left hand toward your right side to bring her in, then extend it to the left to send her. Lead both with the hand, not the shoulders.

variants.title: Sit Break to Hip Twist Side Pass
variants.reason: the chart keeps the man's weight on his right foot while the left foot extends or the position is held, and the game's step model cannot dance a step on the supporting foot

figures.name: Curl
figures.summary: After a sit break, the lady curls left under the man's raised hand into a cross-body position and the couple close up.
figures.tip: Be quiet while she curls; your job is a steady hand and a still body. Finish in closed hold ready for a basic.

variants.title: Curl
variants.reason: the chart keeps the man's weight on his right foot while the left foot extends or the position is held, and the game's step model cannot dance a step on the supporting foot

figures.name: Overturned Release to Swivels
figures.summary: An overturned release of the basic ending, leading the lady through a series of swivels while the man sits over the right leg.
figures.tip: Practice the hand rotation slowly: palm down, palm up, palm down. After the swivels return to the basic.

variants.title: Overturned Release to Swivels
variants.reason: the chart keeps the man's weight on his right foot while the left foot extends or the position is held, and the game's step model cannot dance a step on the supporting foot

figures.name: Cross-Body Lead w/ Syncopated UAT L.
figures.summary: A cross-body lead in which the lady's underarm turn to the left is syncopated, so her turn is danced in quicker steps than the plain figure. A Silver level figure.
figures.tip: Settle the plain cross-body lead first, then add the extra steps; keep your hand level as she turns so the syncopation reads as a clear signal.

variants.title: Cross-Body Lead w/ Syncopated UAT L.
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Underarm Pass w/ Syncopated UAT L.
figures.summary: An underarm pass whose finishing underarm turn to the left for the lady is syncopated. It builds on the Bronze underarm pass.
figures.tip: Do not rush the pass itself; take the extra weight changes only in the final turn and finish with your frame ready for the next move.

figures.name: Promenade & CPP Runs
figures.summary: Running steps in promenade and counter-promenade position, travelling side by side across the floor. A Silver level figure.
figures.tip: Run on soft knees with small, even steps and keep your shoulder line toward her; turn the head to match her in each position.

figures.name: Catch & Release
figures.summary: A figure where the man catches the lady's movement and then releases her into the next shape. A Silver level figure.
figures.tip: Keep your arm tone steady through the catch so she has something firm to answer; release only on the count the figure gives.

variants.title: Catch & Release

figures.name: Rudolf Ronde
figures.summary: A figure built around a ronde, a sweeping circle drawn on the floor with the free leg, and one of the showiest Bolero actions.

figures.name: Pivots

figures.name: Bolero Variation 1
figures.summary: A long Gold routine: half basic to open, a sit break and basic, a ronde, an underarm turn with overturn, shadow runs and turns, and a cross-body finish back to the basic.

figures.name: Bolero Variation 2

variants.title: Bolero Variation 2

figures.name: Bolero Variation 3

figures.tip: Keep the dip a gentle lean, never a drop, and make sure the lady has chosen to wrap her leg before you take her weight.

mambo.name: Mambo
mambo.music: Fast, bright Latin music with a driving pulse; the dance starts on the second beat and lets the fourth beat run into a held first.
mambo.movement_tip: Break on 2, keep each step small and quick, and let the hips settle sideways as every step takes weight. Pause through the held 1 instead of stepping on it.
mambo.position_tip: Closed hold and open facing with one or two hands are the home positions. Side-by-side crossovers, fallaway and promenade shapes, and apart-facing chases appear along the way.

figures.name: Mambo Basic
figures.summary: The home figure of Mambo: a forward break and a backward break, each rocking and then stepping aside with a held first beat.
figures.tip: Drill it until the break on 2 is automatic; it can follow or lead almost every Bronze figure, and it is the figure you return to between patterns.

followed_by.name: Open Break & Underarm Turn to R.
Back Spot Turn w/ Underarm Turn to L.

preceded_by.name: Open Break & Underarm Turn to R.

figures.name: Progressive Basic
figures.summary: The basic with the side steps swapped for straight forward-and-back ones, so the pair stays in line like a mirror.
figures.tip: Use it after a Mambo Basic to warm up the breaks, and as the base for the Man's Underarm Turn and the Chase.

figures.name: Side Breaks
figures.summary: A basic danced sideways: each break goes to the side and the feet close on the held count.
figures.tip: Keep the side steps small and stay on the balls of the feet; it goes after a Mambo Basic and returns to it.

figures.name: Open Break & Underarm Turn to R.
figures.summary: From closed hold you break back to open facing, then send her under your raised left hand in a right turn while you break back again.
figures.tip: Release the back hand on the first break and raise the left hand a beat before her turn; follow it with a Mambo Basic or a Crossover Break.

variants.title: Open Break & Underarm Turn to R.

figures.name: Fifth Position Breaks
figures.summary: A basic where each break is a small step back into a fallaway shape, first on one side of the couple and then on the other.
figures.tip: Keep the break steps tiny and the knees soft; it sits between Mambo Basics and works well before the Crossover Breaks.

figures.name: Crossover Breaks Forward
figures.summary: A side-by-side break: both partners turn a quarter, rock forward together, turn back to face, and then repeat to the other side.
figures.tip: Take the hand hold for the side you are going to and change it on the step to face; it follows a Mambo Basic and leads to Crossover Breaks Back or Crossover Turns.

figures.name: Crossover Breaks Back
figures.summary: The backward twin of the Crossover Break: side by side, both break back, then turn to face and step aside.
figures.tip: Change hands as you turn to face, and keep the rock back small; it alternates with Crossover Breaks Forward and returns to a basic.

figures.name: Crossover Turns
figures.summary: Each partner dances a full turn on the spot, in opposite directions, and meets face to face again before turning the other way.
figures.tip: Let the hands go while you turn and pick them up on the held count; it follows the Crossover Breaks and finishes ready for a basic.

figures.name: Fallaway Rock & Swivel
figures.summary: A longer figure that mixes a fallaway break, a swivel on the spot and a walk forward in promenade before closing.
figures.tip: Do the swivel with a quick twist of the heel on the 1 instead of a step; it follows the Mambo Basic and goes back to it.

figures.name: Cross Body Lead
figures.summary: She crosses in front of you as you turn left out of her path, and finishes turned a half turn around to face you again.
figures.tip: Dance a Mambo Basic first so the break is rhythmic, then lead the cross with the left hand and turn left; it also begins several other patterns, such as the Half Moon.

figures.name: Stop & Go
figures.summary: She turns left, is stopped by a check, and then turns right, all under your raised left hand in open facing position.
figures.tip: Keep the left hand quiet at waist height until the lift and lower it at the end of each turn; it follows a Mambo Basic and ends ready to repeat or to open into a crossover.

figures.name: Underarm Pass
figures.summary: She walks forward beneath your raised hand while you turn half right, and you both end in open facing position.
figures.tip: Prepare with a clear lift of the left hand on the held count; come in from a Mambo Basic and go out with a Crossover Break or another open figure.

figures.name: Back Pass
figures.summary: She slides behind your back as you turn left, so that you both finish in closed hold.
figures.tip: Set her right hand on your waist at the start of the turn and keep the left arm raised over her path; it follows a Mambo Basic and can be followed by any closed figure.

figures.name: Man's Underarm Turn
figures.summary: The leader turns under his own raised hand while the lady keeps dancing, and the turn is followed either by a Progressive Basic or by a Cross Body Lead.
figures.tip: Raise the hand before the first step and keep it steady; it follows a Mambo Basic and continues with a basic or crossing figure.

variants.title: Man's Underarm Turn to Cross-Body Lead
variants.reason: the site numbers its last row 5-6 although it lists three steps (the Cross-Body Lead steps 4-6), so the chart cannot be matched step for step; the Cross Body Lead after the turn is already a figure of its own

figures.name: Traveling Underarm Turn to R.
figures.summary: An underarm turn with a Cuban cross behind: she makes a turn and a half to the right while you cross behind and travel half right.
figures.tip: Prepare with a clear lift of the left hand and circle it over her head on the cross; follow a Mambo Basic and finish with a Crossover Break or a basic.

figures.name: Turnstile
figures.summary: The lady spins freely to the right, more than a full turn, while you step diagonally forward and turn left to meet her.
figures.tip: Give a single clear push with the right hand and let go; it follows a Mambo Basic and ends apart or in open hold, ready to take the hand again.

figures.name: Back Spot Turn
figures.summary: A continuous turn on the spot in closed hold, built from a crossed-behind step and a side step, with two short endings and a version in which she turns left.
figures.tip: Keep the steps tiny and the frame still so the turn comes from your body; dance it from a Mambo Basic, use one of the endings to leave, and try the version with the left turn once the plain turn is steady.

variants.title: Back Spot Turn w/ Underarm Turn to L.

figures.name: Forward Spot Turn
figures.summary: The spot turn the other way: the leader steps forward while turning left, and the lady crosses behind in a mirror of the Back Spot Turn.
figures.tip: Keep the turn tiny and slow down the shoulders so she can follow; it follows a Mambo Basic and flows into the Back Spot Turn.

figures.name: Spot Turn in Two Directions
figures.summary: A forward spot turn left, an easing step across her side, and a back spot turn right, so the couple turns in two directions without leaving the spot.
figures.tip: Take the middle bar slowly so she can change direction with you; it follows a Forward Spot Turn or a basic and ends ready for a basic.

figures.name: Half Circle
figures.summary: She winds into a cuddle shape on your right as you turn, and then unwinds in a right turn while you finish in open hold.
figures.tip: Keep the two hands low through the wrap and raise the left hand only for her unwind; it follows a Mambo Basic and ends in open facing.

figures.name: Half Moon
figures.summary: A cross body lead that winds into sweetheart on your side, rocks forward and back, and then unwinds in a full turn to the right.
figures.tip: Keep the joined right hands low and the circle smooth; you can add a second rock in sweetheart. It follows a Mambo Basic and ends in open hold.

figures.name: Chase
figures.summary: A playful pattern danced apart: first a plain Progressive Basic, then versions in which you walk away from her and she follows, with half or full turns.
figures.tip: Hold a steady distance, keep the progressive basic rhythm and smile; it follows and returns to a Mambo Basic.

variants.title: Chase Half Turns
variants.reason: partners dance apart with no hold for two bars while one walks away from the other, which the game's holds cannot show

variants.title: Chase Full Turn
variants.reason: partners dance apart with no hold for two bars while one walks away from the other, which the game's holds cannot show

figures.name: Open Left Turn
figures.summary: An open-position turn in which the lady turns left while the leader keeps the mambo rhythm going beside her.
figures.tip: Learn the Mambo Basic and underarm turns first, and lift the hand early so she has time to turn.

variants.title: Open Left Turn
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Crossover Side Breaks
figures.summary: A crossover figure that adds side breaks between the side-by-side breaks, so the pair swaps from crossing to facing several times.
figures.tip: Be fluent in the Crossover Breaks forward and back before you try it, and keep each step small.

variants.title: Crossover Side Breaks
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Fifth Position Side Breaks
figures.summary: The Fifth Position Breaks with a side break added, so each fallaway break is followed by a short step aside.
figures.tip: Make the back steps tiny; it grows from the Fifth Position Breaks and the Side Breaks you already know.

variants.title: Fifth Position Side Breaks
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Cross-Body Lead w/ UAT L.
