wcs.name: West Coast Swing
wcs.music: Smooth, bluesy pop, R&B and contemporary tracks with a steady, laid-back groove.
wcs.movement_tip: Travel along a narrow slot, with the follower walking down it while the leader steps aside to let her pass; keep the knees soft and the movement stretchy and grounded.
wcs.position_tip: Mostly open facing hold with one or two hands joined; hold some tone in the arms so the connection can compress on the walks and stretch on the send-out.

figures.name: Starter Step
figures.summary: The pattern that usually opens a West Coast dance: two side triples in closed hold, finishing in a back rock.
figures.tip: Treat it as the opening move; the closed whips, the throwout and the closed tuck-in all follow it, so keep the final step small to set up the next figure.

variants.title: Starter Step

figures.name: Throwout

figures.tip: Turn your body left as she passes instead of pushing her with the arm; dance it straight after the starter step or a closed whip.

figures.name: Underarm Pass
figures.summary: A basic pass in which the leader raises his left hand and the follower walks beneath it.
figures.tip: Raise the left hand on 2 and keep it still; finish the lowering on the first step of the anchor so she never ducks.

figures.name: Left Side Pass
figures.summary: The simplest pass: the leader turns left and the follower walks down the slot along his left side.
figures.tip: Step off the slot on 2 so her lane is open; follow it with a sugarpush or a whip to keep the six-count rhythm going.

figures.name: Sugarpush
figures.summary: The core six-count pattern of the dance, where the follower is drawn in and then sent back down the slot.
figures.tip: Feel the compression on 2 before you send her out on 3a4; add a full right turn for her as the first variation.

figures.name: Right Side Pass
figures.summary: A two-pass pattern in which the leader changes hands after the first pass and passes her a second time.
figures.tip: Plan the hand change during the first anchor, since a late swap makes the second pass rushed; keep both anchors at the slot ends.

figures.name: Two-Hand Tuck-In Turn
figures.summary: A pass in which she is stopped with the leader's palm and then turned out beneath his raised hand.
figures.tip: Brace for the whole of 3 and 4 before releasing; dance it after a pass or a sugarpush so both hands are already joined.

figures.name: Whip
figures.summary: The signature West Coast figure: the follower walks in, curves round the leader and is sent back along the slot.
figures.tip: Keep the clockwise turn flowing to count 6; the whip combines well with underarm turns, the locked whip and a plain sugarpush afterwards.

figures.name: 8-Count Closed Whip
figures.summary: The longer, eight-count whip: it begins in open position and finishes in closed hold across the slot.
figures.tip: Finish it exactly in closed hold facing across the slot; either a throwout or a tuck can come next.

lindy.name: Lindy Hop
lindy.music: Fast and medium big band swing, the sound of the Savoy Ballroom.
lindy.movement_tip: Sit low with soft knees and pulse down on every beat. Let the steps stay small and the energy stay in the ground.
lindy.position_tip: Start in closed hold or open facing hold with an elastic connection. The arms stay flexible so she can be drawn in and sent out again.

figures.name: 6-Count Basic
figures.summary: The foundation step of Lindy Hop: a rock step followed by two triple steps, left then right, in six counts. It is danced from closed hold and sets the bounce for everything else.
figures.tip: Sink into the knees and pulse on every count so the triples stay springy. Follow it with a Tuck-In or Underarm Turn, or use the Kick Basic variant for some extra flavour.

figures.name: 8-Count Basic
figures.summary: The eight-count version of the basic: a rock step, a triple, two single steps that turn the couple half round, and a final triple. It introduces the longer phrasing used in the swingout.
figures.tip: Keep the two middle steps small so the rotation is smooth. Dance it after a six-count basic, and move on to a Swingout from Closed once the turn feels easy.

figures.name: Throwout
figures.summary: The simplest way to open out from closed hold: a rock step, a left-turning triple that sends her past you, and an anchor in open facing hold.
figures.tip: Let your body turn do the work, not your arms. Dance it after a closed basic, and then follow with an Underarm Turn, a Tuck-In or any other open figure.

figures.name: Underarm Turn to Right
figures.summary: She turns right under the joined hands while you triple to the side. It is the first underarm turn in the syllabus and is danced from closed or open position.
figures.tip: Raise the left hand on the first triple and keep it steady until she faces you again. Combine it with the Throwout and the Underarm Turn to Left.

figures.name: Underarm Turn to Left
figures.summary: The partner to the turn to the right: she turns left under the raised hands while you rotate half a turn right. Danced from open facing hold with hands joined.
figures.tip: Bring the hand up as she replaces her weight so the turn begins in time. Use it after the Throwout or an Underarm Turn to Right.

figures.name: Closed Tuck-In
figures.summary: From a closed basic you hold her through a triple, then release both hands and let her spin freely to the right while you step away. It ends in open hold.
figures.tip: Keep the left arm braced, then give a clear light push before letting go. Dance it straight after a six-count basic or a Throwout, and follow with the open figures.

figures.name: Open Tuck-In
figures.summary: A tuck-in from open facing hold: after a rock step you raise the joined hands and circle them over her head so she makes one full turn right.
figures.tip: Raise the hands to eye level for a moment before you circle them. It goes well after an Underarm Turn and leads into a Sugarpush or a Swingout.

figures.name: Handshake Tuck-In
figures.summary: The tuck-in danced with right hands joined: you draw her in on the first triple and send her into one full turn right with a circling raised hand.
figures.tip: Use a relaxed handshake grip that can swivel. Dance it from a Flick or Handshake Pass and finish by taking the usual left-right hold.

figures.name: Underarm Pass
figures.summary: A simple pass in open facing hold: you step back and draw her forward, then lift your hand so she travels under it while you rotate a quarter right.
figures.tip: Let your arm form a clear arch before she arrives at it. Use it after the Open Tuck-In or the Sugarpush, and follow it with a basic or a Swingout.

figures.name: Flick / Handshake Pass
figures.summary: A pass from right-to-right handshake hold: you release the hand and she passes in front of you, turning left, before you anchor.
figures.tip: Lead the pass with your body turning right, then let the hand go. It combines with the Handshake Tuck-In and returns to the usual hold on the anchor.

figures.name: Sugarpush
figures.summary: The classic push-and-release pattern: she walks in, is stopped by a firm brace on 3, and springs back as you step forward. A six-count figure from open facing hold.
figures.tip: Build the brace in your arms, not in your shoulders. Dance it after the open basic or a Tuck-In, then follow with an Underarm Turn or a Swingout.

figures.name: Sugarpush w/ Underarm Turn to Right
figures.summary: The sugarpush with a turn: after the stop and the spring back she turns right under the raised hand through the anchor. She finishes facing you in open hold.
figures.tip: Wait until she steps away before you lift the hand. Link it after a Throwout and lead straight into another open figure.

variants.title: Sugarpush w/ Underarm Turn to Right

figures.name: Swingout (from Closed)
figures.summary: The swingout from closed hold: after the rock step you rotate with her through a triple and two single steps, then send her out into open hold. It is Lindy Hop's signature move.
figures.tip: Stay low and make the circle round, not straight. Dance it from the 6-Count or 8-Count Basic, and follow with an open figure such as the Charleston or a Tuck-In.

figures.name: Swingout (from Open)
figures.summary: The eight-count swingout from open hold: she walks in, you take her round in closed hold and send her out again. It is the heart of the dance.
figures.tip: Keep your frame close while she walks in and let the rotation carry her around you. Dance it after an open figure and repeat it or chain it with the Lindy Circle.

figures.name: Swingout w/ Underarm Turn to L.
figures.summary: A swingout in which she unwinds to the left under your raised right hand on the 5-6 instead of walking straight out. It finishes in open facing hold.
figures.tip: Lift the hand after the rotation has finished so she has a clear exit. It follows an open basic or a pass and leads into any open figure.

variants.title: Swingout w/ Underarm Turn to L.

figures.name: Swingout w/ Underarm Turn to R.
figures.summary: A swingout where she spins one and a half turns to the right under your raised right hand during the final steps, ending in open hold.
figures.tip: Keep the hand high and let it circle with her as she spins. Practise it after a plain swingout, and finish by catching her left hand for the anchor.

variants.title: Swingout w/ Underarm Turn to R.

figures.name: Lindy Circle (6-Count)
figures.summary: The six-count version of the Lindy Circle: she walks in from open hold, runs round you and the two of you finish in closed hold across the slot.
figures.tip: Share one centre and keep the circle small. It leads into a closed basic, a Throwout or a Tuck-In and is a handy way to change position.

figures.name: Lindy Circle (8-Count)
figures.summary: The eight-count Lindy Circle: the couple circles through a longer phrase, ending in closed hold after a full anchor. It is a complete circle from open to closed.
figures.tip: Spread the rotation evenly across the eight counts. Try it after a Swingout and then follow with a closed basic.

figures.name: Lindy Circle w/ Underarm Turn to L
figures.summary: A Lindy Circle during which she unwinds under your raised hand before you bring her back into closed hold for the final triple.
figures.tip: Slide the right hand around her back so closed hold is waiting for her. Combine it with the Lindy Circle and a closed basic.

variants.title: Lindy Circle w/ Underarm Turn to L

figures.name: Locked Whip
figures.summary: A circle that wraps her into a loose cuddle at your side, then unwraps her with the pull-back and anchor. It begins and ends in open hold.
figures.tip: Keep the wrap loose and low so she cannot be trapped. Use it after a Swingout from Open and follow with a basic.

figures.name: Reverse Swingout
figures.summary: A swingout danced with a left turn: you rotate counter-clockwise while she walks round you. It mirrors the standard swingout.
figures.tip: Dance it after a closed basic so that the new direction feels fresh. Try it before or after the Reverse Whip.

salsa.name: Salsa

salsa.movement_tip: Keep every step small and quick, land on the ball of the foot and let the heel settle as the weight arrives. Soft knees make the hips move by themselves, so do not add extra hip action.
salsa.position_tip: Stand tall with the weight forward and the partners a little apart in a relaxed hold. Hands are joined at about waist height, in the upper clasp or with his hand underneath, and the arms follow the body instead of being waved around.

figures.name: Salsa Basic

figures.tip: Learn the closed basic first and keep the steps tiny; every other Level I figure is a variation of it, so return to it between patterns and use the open basic to set up turns.

figures.name: Cumbia Basic
figures.summary: A basic that crosses one foot behind the other on each break and finishes with a step to the side, giving a gentle rolling feel.
figures.tip: Practise it alone first so the cross-behind stays small; use it between Salsa Basics for a change of colour.

figures.name: Underarm Turn to R.
figures.summary: The most basic salsa turn: she takes the place of her forward break by turning right under the raised hands, and she ends facing you.
figures.tip: Raise the hand a count before she starts and keep it steady; it follows a Salsa Basic and leads to the Cross Body Lead or a second turn.

figures.name: Underarm Turn to L.
figures.summary: A turn for the lady to her left, taken from the open basic in the second bar. She gets a full turn under the raised hand while you step forward and close.
figures.tip: Lift the right hand at the end of the open basic and lower it as she finishes; it can be followed by another open basic, a Cross Body Lead or the same turn again.

figures.name: Man's Underarm Turn to R.
figures.summary: You turn under the joined hands while she keeps dancing the open basic, and you finish facing her.
figures.tip: Hold the arm firm and a little above her head; step before you turn so the turn comes from the feet. It follows an open basic and leads to a Cross Body Lead.

variants.title: Man's Underarm Turn to R.
variants.reason: the site's chart lists the second bar as one row numbered 4 that stands for steps 4-6 of the Open Basic, so the six game steps cannot be matched row by row against the chart

figures.name: Cross Body Lead
figures.summary: The turning basic that lets the lady cross in front of the man and swap places: you step out of her way and she walks the line you leave.
figures.tip: Turn out of her lane on the third step and keep the left arm as a clear guide; it follows a Salsa Basic and leads to turns such as the Coca Cola.

figures.name: Hand Push Basic
figures.summary: A set of open-position figures built on the open basic, in which the two palms meet and push on the second bar. The variants add a cucaracha side step or a small crossover first.
figures.tip: Keep the hands at chest height and press softly; it follows an Open Basic and can be danced several times in a row before an underarm turn.

figures.name: Stop & Go
figures.summary: She turns left, is stopped by a check, and then turns right, all under your raised left hand from open facing position.
figures.tip: Keep the left hand at waist height until the lift and lower it after each turn; it follows an Open Basic and can lead to a Cross Body Lead.

figures.name: Back Pass
figures.summary: She passes behind your back with her hand on your waist while you turn left, and you both end in closed hold.
figures.tip: Lead the pass with the left hand raised over her path; it follows an Open Basic and is followed by any closed figure, such as a Salsa Basic.

figures.name: Man's Underarm Turn to Cross-Body Lead
figures.summary: You turn under your own raised hand into cross-body position, and she then crosses in front of you in a cross body lead.
figures.tip: Finish the turn on the third step before you lead; it follows an Open Basic and returns to an Open Basic or a Salsa Basic.

variants.title: Man's Underarm Turn to Cross-Body Lead

figures.name: Underarm Turn with Double Head Loop
figures.summary: A right underarm turn for the lady followed by two loops of the hands over heads, one over hers and one over yours, and a return to closed hold.
figures.tip: Plan the hand changes in advance and keep the arms low and soft; it comes after a Salsa Basic and ends ready for any closed figure.

variants.title: Underarm Turn with Double Head Loop

figures.name: Hand Toss
figures.summary: After a right underarm turn for the lady, you toss her hands from one cross-hand hold to the other in two open basics.
figures.tip: Practise the hand change slowly on the spot first; it follows an Open Basic and ends ready to repeat the toss or to lead a turn.

figures.name: Coca Cola
figures.summary: A cross body lead in which the lady finishes with a spinning turn to her left under your raised hand instead of a simple turn.
figures.tip: Make the cross body clear before the lift; it follows a Salsa Basic or a Cross Body Lead and can be danced twice in a row.

figures.name: Underarm Turn to R, Head Loop & Coca Cola
figures.summary: A right underarm turn, a loop of the hands over her head and a Coca Cola, all in one four-bar pattern ending in closed hold.
figures.tip: Break it into its three parts and learn the hand changes before adding the turns; it comes after an Open Basic and is followed by a Salsa Basic.

variants.title: Underarm Turn to R, Head Loop & Coca Cola

figures.name: Hammerlock
figures.summary: She turns right into a wrap with her arm behind her waist, is unwound with a left turn, and the figure runs on through fallaway and promenade shapes into a cross body lead.
figures.tip: Learn the wrap and unwind on their own before adding the ending; it follows an Open Basic and finishes in cross body style ready for a basic.

figures.name: Man's Wrap & Duck Turn
figures.summary: The man turns right and wraps her arm around his neck or waist, then ducks his head under her arm. The neck and waist versions use the same steps with different hands.
figures.tip: Keep the hand frame low and calm while you turn; it follows an Open Basic and returns to one afterwards.

figures.name: Back Spot Turn
figures.summary: A turn on the spot in closed hold in which you cross behind and she steps between your feet; one version starts from an open break.
figures.tip: Keep both partners over their own feet and turn as a unit; it follows a Salsa Basic and returns to a basic when you finish.

variants.title: Open Break to Back Spot Turn

figures.name: Traveling Underarm Turn to R.
figures.summary: A right underarm turn for the lady in which both partners travel, so the pattern moves across the floor.
figures.tip: Learn the standing Underarm Turn to R. first and keep the steps small; it grows from that Level I turn.

variants.title: Traveling Underarm Turn to R.
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Advanced Back Pass
figures.summary: A more advanced version of the back pass, in which the lady moves behind the man's back with extra turns.
figures.tip: Be sure the plain Back Pass is easy, keep the arm still and let her do the travelling.

variants.title: Advanced Back Pass
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Hand Slide
figures.summary: A figure in which the hands slide along each other while the partners travel past one another.
figures.tip: Keep a light, steady contact in the hands so the slide stays smooth; it builds on the Hand Push and Back Pass.

variants.title: Hand Slide
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Shadow Check & Turn
figures.summary: A shadow-position figure with a check and a turn, danced side by side with the lady in front of the man.
figures.tip: Practise the shadow hold on its own first and keep the check small; it grows from the Back Pass.

variants.title: Shadow Check & Turn
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Elbow Push
figures.summary: A push with the elbow that sends the lady away and brings her back with a turn.
figures.tip: Use a small, clear push and let her own steps do the work; it builds on the Hand Push Basic.

variants.title: Elbow Push
variants.reason: the site gives no man's chart for this figure

figures.name: Man's Hook Turn
figures.summary: A man's turn in which her hand is carried over your head to your shoulder and you duck under her arm on the next bar.
figures.tip: Keep the left hand tight to your head while you turn; it follows an Open Basic and returns to one afterwards.

variants.title: Man's Hook Turn
variants.reason: the site's chart text for step 3 is garbled (it begins "eft foot closes"), so the feet of the man's part cannot be read reliably against the chart
